feature_name: Default interactive picker launch
user_story: As a user, I want to run `resume` with no flags so that I get an interactive fuzzy picker of my coding-agent sessions in the current Scope.
expected_behaviour: When neither `--list` nor `--json` is passed, `app::run` calls `run_interactive`, which spawns one discovery thread per configured agent, streams candidates into the Skim picker via a bounded channel, and returns the picker's exit code (src/app.rs, run_interactive at src/app.rs).
how_to_test: cd into a directory with known pi/claude/codex/omp session fixtures and run `resume` with no arguments in a real terminal; observe the Skim picker opens with streamed rows.

feature_name: Optional positional directory argument
user_story: As a user, I want to pass a directory path as the first positional argument so that Scope is derived from that directory instead of my current working directory.
expected_behaviour: `Cli.directory: Option<PathBuf>` (src/cli.rs) is used by `build_scope` as `cli.directory.as_deref().unwrap_or(Path::new("."))` then canonicalized via `scope::canonical_base` (src/app.rs). A nonexistent directory causes `canonical_base` to fail and `run` prints `resume: <error>` and returns EXIT_USAGE (2) (src/app.rs).
how_to_test: Run `resume /path/to/other/worktree --list` and confirm sessions are scoped to that worktree, not cwd; run `resume /nonexistent/path` and confirm exit code 2 with an error message.

feature_name: -U/--up <N|all> explicit upward Scope
user_story: As a user, I want `--up N` so that Scope includes my current directory and up to N ancestor directories, overriding the Git default.
expected_behaviour: `Cli.up: Option<Distance>` parses `N` or `all` via `Distance::FromStr` (src/cli.rs (FromStr body; error string now sourced from errors::E1003.parser_message() at cli.rs)). When set, `build_scope` builds `Direction::Up(distance)` and Scope mode becomes `ScopeMode::Up`, whose `contains` checks `self.base.ancestors().position(...)` is within distance (src/scope.rs (ScopeMode::Up match arm)).
how_to_test: In a nested directory tree `/a/b/c`, run `resume --up 1` from `/a/b/c` and confirm sessions from `/a/b/c` and `/a/b` are included but not `/a` or `/a/b/c/d`.

feature_name: --up all upward Scope to filesystem root
user_story: As a user, I want `--up all` so that every ancestor directory up to `/` is in Scope.
expected_behaviour: `Distance::All` makes `within()` always return true for Up mode (src/scope.rs), so `contains` matches any ancestor of base regardless of distance, per the table-driven test `up all root` (src/scope.rs).
how_to_test: Run `resume --up all` deep inside a directory tree and confirm sessions recorded anywhere from cwd up through `/` appear, but no descendant/sibling sessions do.

feature_name: -D/--down <N|all> explicit downward Scope
user_story: As a user, I want `--down N` so that Scope includes my current directory and descendants up to N path-component edges deep.
expected_behaviour: `Cli.down: Option<Distance>` mirrors `--up`; Scope mode `ScopeMode::Down` uses `candidate.real_path.strip_prefix(&self.base)` and checks the suffix's component count is within distance (src/scope.rs); depth-2 example verified by `down two` test (src/scope.rs).
how_to_test: From a directory with subdirectories 2+ levels deep containing sessions, run `resume --down 2 --list` and confirm only sessions at depth <=2 are listed.

feature_name: --down all downward Scope to every descendant
user_story: As a user, I want `--down all` so that every descendant directory of my current directory is in Scope, including at `/` which is intentionally broad.
expected_behaviour: `Distance::All` in Down mode always satisfies `within()` (src/scope.rs); README explicitly documents that `--down all` at `/` is broad but still directory-derived, not machine-wide (README.md Explicit direction section).
how_to_test: Run `resume --down all` from a shallow directory containing many nested session workspaces and confirm all of them appear regardless of depth.

feature_name: --up and --down are mutually exclusive
user_story: As a user, I want the CLI to reject combining `--up` and `--down` so that I get a clear usage error instead of ambiguous behavior.
expected_behaviour: `Cli::direction_conflict()` checks `up.is_some() && down.is_some()` directly (src/cli.rs); `main()` checks it before `Cli::validate()` or any other dispatch and emits `errors::E1002.report(...).emit()`, printing the documented four-line `ERROR [E1002] CONFLICTING_DIRECTION: ...` / Trigger: / Fix: / Example: block and exiting with code 2 (src/main.rs). No declarative clap `conflicts_with` is used for this pair, so the error text always comes from resume's own catalog, matching `--man`'s ERRORS section exactly.
how_to_test: Run `resume --up 1 --down 2` and confirm clap prints a usage error and exits with code 2.

feature_name: Invalid --up/--down value is a usage error
user_story: As a user, I want a non-numeric, non-'all' value (or a negative number) for `--up`/`--down` to be rejected clearly so that I know I made a typo.
expected_behaviour: `Distance::from_str` returns `Err("expected a non-negative integer or 'all'")` for anything but `all` (case-insensitive) or a parseable non-negative integer (src/cli.rs (returns errors::E1003.parser_message() at cli.rs)); clap surfaces this as exit code 2, tested by `invalid_distance_is_usage_error` (src/cli.rs (test renamed/merged: invalid_distance_and_since_are_usage_errors)).
how_to_test: Run `resume --up -1` and confirm exit code 2 with a usage error mentioning a non-negative integer or 'all'.

feature_name: -a/--agent is repeatable and replaces, not extends, the agent list
user_story: As a user, I want repeated `-a pi -a codex` flags to set the exact agent list used for discovery so that I can narrow which integrations run.
expected_behaviour: `Cli.agent: Vec<OsString>` uses `action = clap::ArgAction::Append` (src/cli.rs (ArgAction::Append)); `effective_options` only falls back to config/defaults when `cli.agent.is_empty()`, otherwise uses exactly the CLI-supplied list (src/app.rs), tested by `repeated_agent_preserves_replacement_list` (src/cli.rs).
how_to_test: Run `resume -a pi -a codex --list` and confirm only pi and codex sessions appear even if config.toml lists all four agents.

feature_name: Unknown agent name in -a/--agent is a usage error
user_story: As a user, I want `resume -a bogus` to fail clearly so that I know 'bogus' is not a supported agent name.
expected_behaviour: `effective_options` checks every requested agent against `cli::SUPPORTED_AGENTS` and returns `Err(format!("unknown agent {agent:?}"))` on the first name that is not in it, so `run` prints `resume: unknown agent "bogus"` and returns EXIT_USAGE (2). The check reads the one shared constant rather than an inline list, so adding an integration cannot leave the validator behind.
how_to_test: Run `resume --list --agent bogus` and confirm exit code 2 and stderr containing `unknown agent "bogus"`.

feature_name: -a/--agent values are lowercased before validation
user_story: As a user, I want `-a PI` or `-a Codex` to work the same as lowercase so that casing mistakes don't cause failures.
expected_behaviour: `effective_options` maps each `OsString` agent via `.to_string_lossy().to_ascii_lowercase()` before validation (src/app.rs (.to_string_lossy().to_ascii_lowercase())).
how_to_test: Run `resume -a PI --list` and confirm it behaves identically to `resume -a pi --list`.

feature_name: --list mode: stable text listing
user_story: As a user, I want `--list` so that discovery completes fully and I get one deterministic terminal-safe text row per session, suitable for scripting or piping.
expected_behaviour: When `cli.list` is true, `run` calls `discover_all` (blocking until every integration thread joins), prints diagnostics to stderr, then `print_list` prints one `picker_candidate(...).display` line per session in `print_list` (src/app.rs, src/app.rs (print_list)); sessions are pre-sorted deterministically by `compare_sessions` inside `discover_all` (src/app.rs).
how_to_test: Run `resume --list` in a directory with known sessions and confirm stable, deterministically ordered rows are printed to stdout with no interactive UI.

feature_name: --json mode: machine-readable v1 output
user_story: As a user, I want `--json` so that I get one machine-parseable JSON document on stdout describing sessions and errors, safe to pipe into `jq`.
expected_behaviour: When `cli.json` is true, `run` calls `discover_all` then `print_json`, which serializes a `JsonOutput { schemaVersion: 1, sessions, errors }` via `serde_json::to_string` and prints exactly one line to stdout (src/app.rs, src/app.rs (print_json)).
how_to_test: Run `resume --json 2>/dev/null | jq.` and confirm exactly one valid JSON document with schemaVersion 1 is printed.

feature_name: --list and --json share the same discover_all path and exit-code logic
user_story: As a user, I want `--list` and `--json` to apply identical Scope/agent filtering and identical exit-code rules so that only the output format differs.
expected_behaviour: Both branches call `discover_all(&options, scope)` then `discovery_exit(&records, &state)` (src/app.rs); only the printer (`print_list` vs `print_json`) differs.
how_to_test: Run `resume --list --agent pi` and `resume --json --agent pi` in the same directory and confirm the same session set (by id) appears in both, only formatted differently.

feature_name: --verbose enables verbose diagnostics
user_story: As a user, I want `--verbose` so that stderr diagnostics include a redacted source path and error chain, not just a category and count.
expected_behaviour: `Cli.verbose: bool` (src/cli.rs) is ORed with `config.verbose` in `effective_options` (src/app.rs (effective_options verbose field)) and threaded to `print_diagnostics(&state, options.verbose)`; `render_diagnostic` appends `redact_path(path)` and `redact_text(chain)` only when `verbose` is true (src/app.rs (print_diagnostics) / 933-951 (render_diagnostic)).
how_to_test: Create a fixture with an intentionally malformed session file, run `resume --list` (no diagnostic path shown) then `resume --verbose --list` (diagnostic path/chain shown), and diff stderr output.

feature_name: --config <PATH> explicit config file path
user_story: As a user, I want `--config /path/to/config.toml` so that I can point resume at a specific configuration file, bypassing XDG/home discovery.
expected_behaviour: `Cli.config: Option<PathBuf>` (src/cli.rs) is passed to `crate::config::load(cli.config.clone())`; `discover_path` returns the explicit path immediately if `Some`, without checking existence (src/config.rs (discover_path)), tested by `explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence` (src/config.rs (explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence)).
how_to_test: Write a config.toml at a nonstandard path and run `resume --config /that/path/config.toml config example`-style check, or run `resume --config /that/path/config.toml --list` and confirm its `agents` field is honored.

feature_name: --confirm-always requests confirmation for every Resume
user_story: As a user, I want `--confirm-always` so that I am prompted to confirm before resuming any session, even a normal-risk one.
expected_behaviour: `Cli.confirm_always: bool` (src/cli.rs) is ORed with `config.confirm_always` in `effective_options` (src/app.rs); `launch::should_confirm` returns true whenever `confirm_always && !no_confirm`, and `launch::risk_reasons` adds a synthetic "confirmation requested" reason when otherwise risk-free (src/launch.rs (risk_reasons/should_confirm), src/launch.rs (risk_reasons)).
how_to_test: Select a normal-risk session via the picker with `resume --confirm-always` and confirm the 'Continue? [y/N]' prompt appears even though the session has no risk flags.

feature_name: --no-confirm suppresses ordinary confirmation only
user_story: As a user, I want `--no-confirm` so that I skip the ordinary confirmation prompt, but I still want to be warned before resuming a genuinely risky session.
expected_behaviour: `should_confirm` computes `risky || (confirm_always && !no_confirm)` (src/launch.rs (should_confirm)): `no_confirm` only cancels the `confirm_always` branch, never the `risky` branch, so risk prompts (Active/BroadWorkspace/WorkspaceChanged/ConflictingMetadata) always still fire, tested by `no_confirm_never_bypasses_risk` (src/launch.rs (no_confirm_never_bypasses_risk)).
how_to_test: Select a session flagged BroadWorkspace (workspace == $HOME or /) via `resume --no-confirm` and confirm the risk confirmation prompt still appears despite --no-confirm.

feature_name: --confirm-always and --no-confirm are mutually exclusive
user_story: As a user, I want the CLI to reject combining `--confirm-always` and `--no-confirm` since they express contradictory intents.
expected_behaviour: `#[arg(long, conflicts_with = "no_confirm")]` on `confirm_always` and the reciprocal on `no_confirm` (src/cli.rs (confirm_always conflicts_with, no_confirm)) make clap reject the combination with exit code 2, tested by `confirmation_conflict_is_usage_error` (src/cli.rs,118-122... actually src/cli.rs 'confirmation_conflict_is_usage_error' test).
how_to_test: Run `resume --confirm-always --no-confirm` and confirm exit code 2 with a clap usage error.

feature_name: --since <duration> filters Sessions by recent activity (relative)
user_story: As a user with many old sessions, I want `--since 7d` to show only Sessions active in the last 7 days, so that I don't have to scroll past stale entries.
expected_behaviour: `Since::from_str` parses `<N><unit>` where unit is m/h/d/w (src/cli.rs, delegating to `crate::time::parse_relative_duration`); `effective_options` resolves it to a cutoff `SystemTime` via `Since::cutoff(now)` (src/app.rs session_at_or_after); `discover_agent` retains only records whose transcript file mtime is at or after the cutoff via `session_at_or_after` (src/app.rs session_at_or_after), applied identically in both `--list`/`--json` and the interactive picker code paths.
how_to_test: Create fixture transcripts for two+ agents, backdate one set of files' mtimes by 1 hour via `File::set_times`, run `resume --json --since 10m` and confirm only recently-modified sessions appear; covered by `since_duration_filters_out_stale_transcripts_across_all_four_agents` in tests/step9_app.rs.

feature_name: config example subcommand prints a complete example TOML
user_story: As a user, I want `resume config example` so that I can see every documented config field and its default in valid TOML, ready to copy into my config file.
expected_behaviour: `Command::Config(ConfigArgs { command: ConfigCommand::Example })` is matched in main.rs before `app::run` is ever called; `resume::cli::config_example()` returns a static string literal listing `agents`, `confirm_always`, `preview`, `preview_position`, `verbose` (src/cli.rs, src/main.rs (Command::Config dispatch)).
how_to_test: Run `resume config example` and confirm the printed TOML matches the fields documented in README.md's Configuration section and parses successfully via `resume --config <(that output)`.
fix_ref: src/cli.rs (config_example): added "opencode" to the example agents list

feature_name: completions bash subcommand
user_story: As a user, I want `resume completions bash` so that I can install shell completion for bash.
expected_behaviour: `Command::Completions { shell: Shell::Bash }` calls `clap_complete::generate(shells::Bash,...)` to stdout before `app::run` executes, so it never loads config or discovers sessions (src/main.rs (Completions match, Bash), docs/completions.md).
how_to_test: Run `resume completions bash` and confirm a valid bash completion script is printed to stdout with no config/discovery side effects (verify no XDG/HOME env access needed by running with HOME unset).

feature_name: completions zsh subcommand
user_story: As a user, I want `resume completions zsh` so that I can install shell completion for zsh.
expected_behaviour: `Shell::Zsh` branch calls `generate(shells::Zsh,...)` (src/main.rs (Zsh generate)); same pre-`app::run` dispatch guarantee as bash.
how_to_test: Run `resume completions zsh` and confirm a valid zsh `_resume` completion function is printed.

feature_name: completions fish subcommand
user_story: As a user, I want `resume completions fish` so that I can install shell completion for fish.
expected_behaviour: `Shell::Fish` branch calls `generate(shells::Fish,...)` (src/main.rs (Fish generate)); subcommand parsing itself tested by `subcommands_parse` (src/cli.rs (subcommands_parse)).
how_to_test: Run `resume completions fish` and confirm a valid fish completion script is printed.

feature_name: Completions/config subcommands dispatch before app startup
user_story: As a user, I want `resume completions bash` and `resume config example` to work even with no HOME, no config file, and no session data present, so that packaging/CI can generate completions safely.
expected_behaviour: `main()` matches `cli.command` for `Config`/`Completions` and returns before ever calling `resume::app::run(cli)` (src/main.rs (app::run only reached in the None arm)); docs/completions.md explicitly states these subcommands 'do not load a config file, derive Scope, or discover/scan Sessions'.
how_to_test: Run `env -i resume completions bash` (fully cleared environment) and confirm it still succeeds and prints a script, with no error about missing HOME or config.

feature_name: Default Scope inside a Git repository includes all worktrees
user_story: As a user working inside a Git repo, I want the default Scope (no --up/--down) to include every Workspace in the main repo and all linked worktrees at any depth, so that I see sessions from any of my worktrees.
expected_behaviour: `build_scope` calls `discover_git_scope(&base, cli.all_worktrees)`; on success it builds `DefaultScope::Git { common_dir, worktrees }`, and `Scope::contains` in `ScopeMode::Git` accepts any candidate whose real path starts with one of `worktrees`, rejecting a candidate whose own Git common directory differs -- which is how a nested independent repository stays out even though it sits inside the tree.
how_to_test: Inside a repo with a linked worktree via `git worktree add`, run `resume --list` from either worktree and confirm sessions recorded under both worktrees appear, while a nested unrelated git repo's sessions are excluded.

feature_name: Default Scope outside Git is the exact current directory only
user_story: As a user working outside any Git repository, I want the default Scope to be just my current real directory, not its children, so that I don't see unrelated sessions.
expected_behaviour: When `discover_git_scope` fails (not a repo), `build_scope` sets `DefaultScope::Exact { git_warning: Some(error) }`, giving `ScopeMode::Exact`, whose `contains` requires `candidate.real_path == self.base` exactly (src/app.rs (DefaultScope::Exact fallback), src/scope.rs (ScopeMode::Exact)), tested by `non_git_fallback_is_exact_and_missing_workspace_is_matched_by_last_known_path` (src/scope.rs) — corrected test name; the CSV previously cited a nonexistent test name.
how_to_test: Run `resume --list` from a plain (non-git) directory containing a session subdirectory and confirm only sessions whose recorded Workspace is exactly that directory appear, not a session in a subdirectory.

feature_name: Git Scope discovery failure is reported, falls back to exact Scope
user_story: As a user, I want a Git failure (e.g. corrupted repo, git binary missing) to degrade gracefully to exact-directory Scope rather than crashing resume.
expected_behaviour: RESOLVED (was flagged as a doc/behavior gap; now fixed and test-backed). `discover_git_scope` errors become `DefaultScope::Exact { git_warning: Some(error.to_string()) }` (src/app.rs, build_scope). That warning IS surfaced as a `Diagnostic` of category `git_scope_discovery_failed` via `scope_warning_diagnostic` (src/app.rs), injected into `DiscoveryState.errors` in BOTH `discover_all` (src/app.rs) and `run_interactive` (src/app.rs), and printed to stderr by `print_diagnostics`/`aggregate_diagnostics` (src/app.rs,892). The category maps to E3002 GIT_SCOPE_DISCOVERY_FAILED in the unified error catalog (src/errors.rs) and is documented at src/man.rs,517. README.md:50 ('A Git failure is reported as a diagnostic.') is now accurate.
how_to_test: Simulate `git` being unavailable (e.g. temporarily rename it off PATH) inside a git repo, run `resume --list`, and confirm resume falls back to exact-directory Scope while stderr shows `resume: git_scope_discovery_failed: 1` (and, with --verbose, the underlying error text). Unit-covered by `git_scope_failure_becomes_a_visible_diagnostic` (src/app.rs), which asserts category, count, non-verbose rendering, and verbose rendering.
fix_ref: src/scope.rs (git_spawn_failed) + (git_command_failed): the verbose chain was a bare OS string ("No such file or directory" when git is not on PATH), which reads as a missing session file. It now names the git subcommand, the directory, and git's own stderr; regression test src/scope.rs (git_scope_failure_names_the_command_and_the_directory)

feature_name: Directory Distance 0 means exactly the current directory
user_story: As a user, I want `--up 0` or `--down 0` to mean exactly the current real directory, matching neither parent nor child.
expected_behaviour: `within(&Distance::Finite(0), edges)` is true only when `edges <= 0`, i.e. `edges == 0`; verified by the table-driven cases `up zero self`/`up zero parent`/`down zero self`/`down zero child` (src/scope.rs (fn within)).
how_to_test: Run `resume --up 0 --list` and `resume --down 0 --list` from a directory with a session recorded exactly there and confirm both include it, while a parent-recorded or child-recorded session is excluded.

feature_name: Scope base and Workspace candidates are canonicalized (symlinks resolved)
user_story: As a user, I want resume to compare real (symlink-resolved) paths so that a symlinked path to my project matches sessions recorded under the real path.
expected_behaviour: `canonical_base` calls `path.canonicalize()` (src/scope.rs (canonical_base)), and `canonical_workspace` does the same for candidate workspaces (src/scope.rs (canonical_workspace)), tested by `canonicalization_resolves_symlinks_and_rejects_missing` (src/scope.rs (canonicalization_resolves_symlinks_and_rejects_missing)).
how_to_test: Create a symlink to a workspace directory, cd through the symlink, and run `resume --list`; confirm sessions recorded under the real (non-symlink) path are still matched.

feature_name: A missing/nonexistent base directory is a usage error
user_story: As a user, I want a clear error if I pass a directory that does not exist so that I don't get a confusing crash.
expected_behaviour: `canonical_base` returns `Err` when `path.canonicalize()` fails on a missing directory; `build_scope`'s caller in `run` prints `resume: <error>` and returns `EXIT_USAGE` (2) (src/app.rs (run build_scope error arm) + src/app.rs (canonical_base call) + src/scope.rs (canonical_base impl)).
how_to_test: Run `resume /this/path/does/not/exist` and confirm exit code 2 with a clear error message.

feature_name: A Session whose recorded Workspace no longer exists is diagnosed as Unavailable, not resumable
user_story: As a user, I want sessions whose recorded directory was deleted or moved to still be listed for diagnosis, but marked Unavailable so I can't accidentally resume into a broken path.
expected_behaviour: `normalize_availability` sets `session.support = SupportStatus::Unavailable` whenever `session.workspace.workspace().is_none_or(|p| !p.is_dir())` (src/app.rs (normalize_availability)), applied after every integration's discovery (src/app.rs,490,537,606 (per-agent call sites)); `status_label` renders it as `UNAVAILABLE` (src/app.rs (status_label, UNAVAILABLE arm)).
how_to_test: Discover a session, then delete its recorded workspace directory, re-run `resume --list`, and confirm the session still appears with status UNAVAILABLE and cannot be selected for resume.

feature_name: --config explicit path has highest precedence
user_story: As a user, I want an explicit `--config <PATH>` to always win over XDG/home discovery, even if the path doesn't exist yet.
expected_behaviour: `discover_path` returns `explicit` immediately whenever `Some`, before checking XDG or home (src/config.rs (discover_path explicit return)), tested by `explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence` (src/config.rs (explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence)); if the explicit file doesn't exist, `load_path` will fail with `ConfigError::Read` when actually loading (src/config.rs (load_path)).
how_to_test: Set XDG_CONFIG_HOME and HOME to point at valid config files with different `agents` lists, then run `resume --config /third/path/config.toml --list` and confirm the third file's settings apply (or a read error if it doesn't exist).

feature_name: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/resume/config.toml precedence over home
user_story: As a user, I want my XDG_CONFIG_HOME config to be used when present, ahead of the ~/.config fallback.
expected_behaviour: `discover_path` checks `xdg.join("resume/config.toml")` via the injected `exists` predicate and returns it if present, before falling back to `home.join(".config/resume/config.toml")` (src/config.rs (discover_path xdg check)), tested by `explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence` (src/config.rs (explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence)).
how_to_test: Create both `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/resume/config.toml` and `~/.config/resume/config.toml` with different `agents` lists, run `resume --list` with no `--config`, and confirm the XDG file's settings apply.

feature_name: ~/.config/resume/config.toml is used only when XDG config is absent
user_story: As a user without XDG_CONFIG_HOME configured (or without a resume config under it), I want resume to fall back to ~/.config/resume/config.toml.
expected_behaviour: `discover_path` only returns the home path when the XDG path (if any) does not exist per the `exists` predicate (src/config.rs (discover_path home fallback)), tested by `explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence` (src/config.rs (explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence)).
how_to_test: Unset XDG_CONFIG_HOME (or ensure no resume config exists under it), create only `~/.config/resume/config.toml`, and confirm `resume --list` applies its settings.

feature_name: Exactly one config file is loaded; files are never merged
user_story: As a user, I want resume to load a single config file deterministically rather than silently merging multiple sources, so config behavior is predictable.
expected_behaviour: `discover_path` returns the first matching path by precedence and `load` loads only that one file via `load_path` (src/config.rs (discover_path returns first match)); README.md's Configuration section states 'Exactly one file is loaded; files are not merged.'
how_to_test: Create differing config.toml files at explicit/XDG/home locations and confirm only the highest-precedence one's fields take effect, with no merged fields from the others.

feature_name: Unknown TOML fields are rejected
user_story: As a user, I want a typo'd config field (e.g. from an old or unsupported option) to fail loudly rather than being silently ignored.
expected_behaviour: `Config` derives `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` (src/config.rs (#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)])), so any field not in {agents, confirm_always, preview, preview_position, verbose} causes `toml::from_str` to fail, surfaced as `ConfigError::Parse`, tested by `unknown_and_invalid_fields_are_rejected` for `mystery = true` (src/config.rs (unknown_and_invalid_fields_are_rejected) + (parse_error_message_includes_line_and_field_detail)).
how_to_test: Write a config.toml containing `mystery = true`, run `resume --config <that file> --list`, and confirm it fails with a usage error rather than silently ignoring the field.

feature_name: Invalid enum/type values in config are rejected
user_story: As a user, I want an invalid `preview_position` or `preview` value to fail clearly instead of silently falling back to a default.
expected_behaviour: `PreviewMode`/`PreviewPosition` derive `Deserialize` with `#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]` and only accept `hidden`/`visible` or `auto`/`right`/`bottom` respectively (src/config.rs (PreviewMode), (PreviewPosition)); an invalid value like `preview_position = 'left'` fails `toml::from_str`, tested by `unknown_and_invalid_fields_are_rejected` (src/config.rs (unknown_and_invalid_fields_are_rejected)).
how_to_test: Write a config.toml with `preview_position = 'left'`, run `resume --config <that file> --list`, and confirm it fails with a parse/usage error.

feature_name: Config-level 'since' field accepts the same duration|date|all syntax as --since
user_story: As a user, I want to set a default `since` cutoff in config.toml so I don't have to pass --since on every invocation, and have --since on the CLI override it when I do.
expected_behaviour: `Config.since: Option<Since>` deserializes via `deserialize_since`, reusing `Since::from_str` so config and CLI accept identical syntax and reject the same malformed inputs (src/config.rs); `effective_options` prefers `cli.since` over `config.since` when both are present (src/app.rs), mirroring the -a/--agent override pattern.
how_to_test: Write a config.toml with `since = '7d'`, run `resume --config <path> --list` with no --since flag and confirm the 7-day cutoff applies; run again with `--since all` on the CLI and confirm it overrides the config value; covered by `documented_field_set_loads`/`since_all_and_date_load_from_config` in src/config.rs.

feature_name: The full documented field set loads and applies correctly
user_story: As a user, I want every field shown in `resume config example` (agents, confirm_always, verbose, preview, preview_position) to actually parse and take effect together.
expected_behaviour: `documented_field_set_loads` test writes all five fields and asserts each parses into the expected `Config` value (src/config.rs (documented_field_set_loads)); this exact field set matches `cli::config_example()` (src/cli.rs (config_example, now six fields incl. since)).
how_to_test: Write a config.toml with all five fields set to non-default values, run `resume --config <that file> --list` (or introspect via effective_options-adjacent behavior), and confirm each field's effect (agent list, confirm prompts, verbose diagnostics).

feature_name: Default agent list when neither -a nor config.agents is set
user_story: As a user with no config and no -a flags, I want resume to discover sessions from all four supported agents by default.
expected_behaviour: `effective_options` falls back to `vec!["codex", "claude", "pi", "omp"]` when `cli.agent` is empty and `config.agents` is `None` (src/app.rs (within effective_options)).
how_to_test: With no config file and no -a flags, run `resume --list` and confirm sessions from pi, claude, codex, and omp fixtures all appear (as in tests/step9_app.rs `json_discovers_all_four_and_stdout_is_only_schema`).

feature_name: config confirm_always field behaves like the CLI flag
user_story: As a user, I want to set `confirm_always = true` in my config file so that I don't need to pass `--confirm-always` on every invocation.
expected_behaviour: `effective_options` computes `confirm_always: cli.confirm_always || config.confirm_always.unwrap_or(false)` (src/app.rs), so a config-level true has the same effect as the CLI flag.
how_to_test: Set `confirm_always = true` in config.toml, resume a normal-risk session with no CLI flags, and confirm the confirmation prompt appears.

feature_name: config verbose field behaves like the CLI flag
user_story: As a user, I want to set `verbose = true` in my config so verbose diagnostics are always on without passing --verbose each time.
expected_behaviour: `effective_options` computes `verbose: cli.verbose || config.verbose.unwrap_or(false)` (src/app.rs).
how_to_test: Set `verbose = true` in config.toml, trigger a diagnostic condition, run `resume --list` with no CLI --verbose flag, and confirm verbose-style output (path/chain) appears on stderr.

feature_name: config preview field controls picker preview visibility default
user_story: As a user, I want `preview = "visible"` in my config to start the picker with the preview pane already shown.
expected_behaviour: `effective_options` reads `preview: config.preview.unwrap_or(PreviewMode::Hidden)` (src/app.rs) and passes it into `run_production_picker`, which sets the `:hidden` suffix on `preview_window` only when `mode == PreviewMode::Hidden` (src/picker.rs (build_production_options; :hidden visibility, preview_window)).
how_to_test: Set `preview = "visible"` in config.toml, launch the interactive picker, and confirm the preview pane is visible immediately without pressing Ctrl-O.

feature_name: config preview_position field (auto/right/bottom)
user_story: As a user, I want to control whether the preview pane renders to the right or below the list, or let resume decide automatically based on terminal width.
expected_behaviour: `build_production_options` maps `PreviewPosition::Right`->"right", `Bottom`->"down", and `Auto` picks "right" only when `tty_size()` width >= 100, else "down" (src/picker.rs (PreviewPosition match) + (preview_window); tty_size at).
how_to_test: In a wide terminal (>=100 cols) with `preview_position = "auto"`, confirm the preview renders on the right; in a narrower terminal, confirm it renders at the bottom; then force `preview_position = "bottom"` in a wide terminal and confirm it still renders at the bottom.

feature_name: config example output round-trips as valid config
user_story: As a user, I want the output of `resume config example` to be a valid config file I can save directly, so copy-paste always works.
expected_behaviour: `config_example()`'s literal TOML uses only fields accepted by `Config`'s `deny_unknown_fields` schema, and its `agents` array lists every entry of `cli::SUPPORTED_AGENTS`. Both halves matter: the example is the template users copy into config.toml, so an unknown field makes the copied file fail to load and a missing agent silently turns that integration off. `config_example_round_trips_through_config_schema` compares the list against SUPPORTED_AGENTS rather than a hand-written copy, so a new integration cannot drift out of the example.
how_to_test: Run `resume config example > /tmp/c.toml && resume --config /tmp/c.toml --list` and confirm it loads without a config error.
fix_ref: src/cli.rs (config_example) + (config_example_round_trips_through_config_schema): the test now compares the example list against SUPPORTED_AGENTS instead of a hand-written copy, so a new integration cannot drift out again

feature_name: Preview pane is hidden by default
user_story: As a user, I want the picker to start with the preview pane hidden so my terminal isn't cluttered until I ask for it.
expected_behaviour: `build_production_options` appends `:hidden` to `preview_window` whenever `mode != PreviewMode::Visible` (i.e. the default `PreviewMode::Hidden`) (src/picker.rs (build_production_options)); the spike's `build_options` also documents `preview_window = "right:60%:hidden"` (src/picker.rs).
how_to_test: Launch `resume` with no config/flags in a fresh terminal and confirm the preview pane is not visible until Ctrl-O is pressed.

feature_name: Ctrl-O toggles Preview visibility
user_story: As a user, I want Ctrl-O to show/hide the preview pane on demand so I can inspect session details without permanently splitting my screen.
expected_behaviour: `build_options`/`build_production_options` bind `"ctrl-o:toggle-preview"` (src/picker.rs (build_options), (build_production_options)), Skim's native `toggle-preview` action; regression-tested end-to-end by `preview_hidden_by_default_and_ctrl_o_toggles` (tests/picker_spike.rs), which asserts preview is hidden initially, shown after one Ctrl-O (`\x0f`), and hidden again after a second Ctrl-O.
how_to_test: In the interactive picker, press Ctrl-O once and confirm the preview pane appears; press it again and confirm it disappears.

feature_name: Ctrl-R is intentionally a no-op (never reloads/rescans)
user_story: As a user, I want Ctrl-R to do nothing rather than accidentally triggering a filesystem scan, since Skim's default `reload` action would run `find` on the working directory when items come from a channel.
expected_behaviour: `build_options`/`build_production_options` bind `"ctrl-r:ignore"` (src/picker.rs (build_options, FINDING comment), (production)) instead of `reload`; the code comment documents the FINDING that channel-fed Skim's `reload` without an argument re-runs the default `find` command, which is unacceptable, and the accepted fallback is the dual-section preview; regression-tested by `ctrl_r_does_not_scan_filesystem` (tests/picker_spike.rs (ctrl_r_does_not_scan_filesystem)).
how_to_test: In the interactive picker, press Ctrl-R and confirm nothing visibly changes (no re-scan, no filesystem listing appears in the candidate list).

feature_name: Esc cancels without resuming, exit code 0
user_story: As a user, I want to press Esc to back out of the picker cleanly without resuming any session, restoring my terminal.
expected_behaviour: Both `build_options` and `build_production_options` bind `"esc:abort"`; `classify` maps an abort outcome whose final key is not Ctrl-C to `PickerOutcome::Cancelled` (src/picker.rs (classify abort arm)); `run_interactive` maps `Cancelled` to `EXIT_OK` (0) unless zero sessions/integrations succeeded, in which case `EXIT_ERROR` (src/app.rs); regression-tested by `esc_cancels_and_restores_terminal` asserting exit 0 (tests/picker_spike.rs).
how_to_test: Launch the interactive picker with at least one discoverable session, press Esc, and confirm the process exits 0 with the terminal restored and no session resumed.

feature_name: Ctrl-C interrupts the picker, exit code 130
user_story: As a user, I want Ctrl-C to interrupt the picker distinctly from Esc, using the conventional SIGINT-style exit code 130, so scripts can detect a hard interrupt.
expected_behaviour: `classify` checks `is_interrupt(&output.final_key)` which matches `SkimKey::Ctrl('c')` and returns `PickerOutcome::Interrupted` (src/picker.rs (classify) + (is_interrupt)); `run_interactive` maps `Interrupted` directly to `EXIT_INTERRUPT` = 130 (src/app.rs (EXIT_INTERRUPT const) + (Interrupted arm)); regression-tested by `ctrl_c_exits_130` (tests/picker_spike.rs).
how_to_test: Launch the interactive picker and press Ctrl-C; confirm the process exits with code 130 (`echo $?` after exit).

feature_name: Terminal smaller than 60x10 fails preflight before picker starts
user_story: As a user with an undersized terminal window, I want resume to fail with a clear error before Skim even attempts to render, rather than crashing or rendering garbled output.
expected_behaviour: `preflight()` reads terminal size via ioctl `TIOCGWINSZ` on `/dev/tty` and returns `Err("terminal too small: WxH (minimum 60x10)")` when `w < MIN_TERM_WIDTH (60) || h < MIN_TERM_HEIGHT (10)` (src/picker.rs, size guard; constants at src/picker.rs); `run_interactive` surfaces this as `PickerOutcome::PreflightFailed`, printed to stderr, mapped to `EXIT_USAGE` (2) at src/app.rs — the same exit code (2) the standalone spike example uses, so there is no production/spike discrepancy.
how_to_test: Resize a terminal (or spawn a PTY) to 40 columns x 8 rows, run `resume` interactively, and confirm it fails fast with a 'terminal too small' message and exit code 2 rather than attempting to render.

feature_name: No controlling terminal (/dev/tty unavailable) fails preflight
user_story: As a user running resume in a context with no TTY (e.g. certain CI/automation contexts), I want a clear preflight failure rather than a confusing panic.
expected_behaviour: `preflight()` first attempts to open `/dev/tty` read+write and returns `Err("no controlling terminal (/dev/tty: <io error>)")` if that fails, before checking size (src/picker.rs).
how_to_test: Run `resume` (no --list/--json) in an environment where /dev/tty cannot be opened (e.g. certain detached/daemonized process contexts) and confirm a clear 'no controlling terminal' error rather than a crash.

feature_name: Picker operates via /dev/tty independent of redirected stdin
user_story: As a user piping data into resume's stdin for another purpose, I want the interactive picker to still work because it talks to /dev/tty directly, not fd 0.
expected_behaviour: Skim opens `/dev/tty` directly via `get_tty()`, independent of stdin, per the spike module doc table ('No control terminal / tiny terminal fail before start' / '/dev/tty operation under redirected stdin' rows) (src/picker.rs (doc-table row)); regression-tested by the redirected-stdin PTY test which sends Enter through the PTY (the tty) while stdin is otherwise redirected (tests/picker_spike.rs area near offset 600-620).
how_to_test: Run `resume < /dev/null` (or with stdin piped from an unrelated source) inside a PTY and confirm the picker still opens and accepts keystrokes via the terminal.

feature_name: Preview shows both normalized and raw-but-terminal-safe sections
user_story: As a user inspecting a session's preview, I want to see both a normalized (whitespace-folded) version and a closer-to-raw (still terminal-safe) version of the content, since Ctrl-R can't switch live views.
expected_behaviour: `PreviewStore::render` always includes a `# normalized` section and, when `show_raw` is set, a `# raw (still terminal-safe, unfiltered)` section too; `run_production_picker` sets `store.show_raw.store(true,...)` unconditionally so production Preview always shows both sections (src/picker.rs (PreviewStore::render, raw section), (run_production_picker sets show_raw=true)); `picker_candidate` builds the same dual-section text directly for the production picker (src/app.rs).
how_to_test: Open the preview pane (Ctrl-O) on any session in the interactive picker and confirm both a '# normalized' and a '# raw' section are present in the preview text.

feature_name: Picker/list row format is UPDATED AGENT[PROFILE] TITLE BRANCH
user_story: As a user scanning the picker or --list output, I want a consistent column layout so I can quickly compare sessions by recency, agent, title, and branch.
expected_behaviour: `picker_candidate` formats `format!("{:<10} {:<18} {} {}", updated, agent, title, branch)` where `title` is truncated and padded to a terminal-derived width via `text::pad_to_width`/`text::truncate_to_width` so `branch` always starts at a fixed column, and `agent` includes `[profile]` when present via `agent_label` (src/app.rs (picker_candidate), (agent_label)); `print_list` reuses the identical `picker_candidate(...).display` string for `--list` (src/app.rs), and the picker header reads `UPDATED AGENT[PROFILE] TITLE BRANCH` (src/picker.rs). There is no STATUS or WORKSPACE column in either surface.
how_to_test: Run `resume --list --agent pi` and visually confirm four left-to-right columns: relative update time, `agent[profile]`, a fixed-width title, then branch; confirm the picker's header line matches.

feature_name: Branch column shows the real Git branch via `git symbolic-ref`, not a placeholder
user_story: As a user reading the picker/list row, I want the BRANCH column to reflect the Session's actual recorded Workspace branch, so I can tell sessions on different branches apart at a glance.
expected_behaviour: `branch_label` resolves and process-wide caches (keyed by the Workspace path exactly as supplied to it, not canonicalized) the result of `resolve_branch_label`, which runs `git -C <workspace> symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD`; a clean branch name wins, a detached-but-inside-a-worktree HEAD renders `detached`, and no Workspace or a non-Git/failed lookup renders `no-branch` (src/app.rs).
how_to_test: Run `resume --list` on a session recorded inside a git worktree on a named branch and confirm the BRANCH column shows that exact branch name, not a placeholder; check a session with no recorded Workspace shows `no-branch`.

feature_name: Selection resolves via opaque CandidateKey, never a row index or display string
user_story: As a user, I want my selection to remain correct even if late-arriving candidates reorder the visible rows while I'm typing a filter, so I never accidentally resume the wrong session.
expected_behaviour: `SkimItem::output()` returns only `format!("key:{}", self.key.0)` (src/picker.rs); `classify` downcasts the selected item back to its `CandidateKey` (src/picker.rs (classify downcast)); `resume_selected` looks the key up in a `HashMap<CandidateKey, CandidateRecord>` (src/app.rs (run_interactive HashMap lookup)); regression-tested by `candidate_key_is_opaque_identity` and the demo PTY test asserting the emitted key is one of the known keys, never a path (src/picker.rs (candidate_key_is_opaque_identity) — CSV previously cited an impossible line number beyond the 788-line file; tests/picker_spike.rs ~300-312).
how_to_test: Stream several candidates into the picker while typing a filter that changes visible order, select one, and confirm the resumed session matches the one you actually highlighted, not a stale row position.

feature_name: Risk confirmation prompt for an Active session
user_story: As a user, I want the risk-confirmation logic to warn before resuming a Session marked Active, while documentation accurately states that v0.1.0 discovery cannot currently produce Active evidence.
expected_behaviour: `risk_reasons` adds `Session is Active` and `should_confirm` returns true for a Session with `ActivityStatus::Active` (src/launch.rs). Active is now REACHABLE in production for two of the four integrations: Codex, via the shared process-first `lsof` open-rollout probe (src/integration/codex/activity.rs, wired once before discovery in src/app.rs); and OMP, via `correlate_live_with`'s live-process+TTY+fresh-breadcrumb correlation (src/integration/omp/activity.rs,169-211, wired in src/app.rs). Pi and Claude still report Unknown by default (no live-correlation evidence path exists for them in v0.1.0).
how_to_test: Construct a Session with `ActivityStatus::Active` and confirm the Risk line includes 'Session is Active' (unit-level, src/launch.rs). For real coverage: hold a Codex rollout open with a live `codex` process and select it via the picker; confirm the risk prompt fires and cannot be bypassed with --no-confirm (`no_confirm_never_bypasses_risk`, src/launch.rs). No end-to-end test currently selects a genuinely live Active session through the real picker (E2E gap).

feature_name: Risk confirmation prompt for BroadWorkspace ($HOME or /)
user_story: As a user, I want to be warned before resuming a session whose recorded Workspace is my entire home directory or filesystem root, since resuming there could be surprising.
expected_behaviour: `broad_workspace_risk` sets `RiskStatus::BroadWorkspace` when `workspace == Path::new("/") || workspace == home` (src/scope.rs), applied by every integration's discovery (`session.risk = crate::scope::broad_workspace_risk(...)` in claude/codex/omp discovery, src/app.rs (claude), (codex); pi/omp use `risk_status` similarly); `risk_reasons` surfaces `"Workspace is broad"` (src/launch.rs).
how_to_test: Discover a session whose recorded cwd is exactly $HOME (or /), select it, and confirm the risk prompt shows 'Workspace is broad'.

feature_name: RiskStatus::WorkspaceChanged is modeled but never assigned by current discovery
user_story: As a user, I expect a documented WorkspaceChanged risk category to exist for sessions whose workspace evidence has changed since discovery, but no current integration actually assigns this status (it is caught separately by revalidate-before-exec).
expected_behaviour: `RiskStatus::WorkspaceChanged` exists in the enum and `risk_reasons` handles it (src/session.rs, src/launch.rs), but grep across all four integrations shows no discovery path ever constructs it — WorkspaceChanged as a *risk* is currently unreachable; the equivalent real-world case is instead caught at exec time by `launch::revalidate` returning `RevalidationError::WorkspaceChanged` (src/launch.rs), independently of this risk field (documented as a known gap in docs/review/round-1-sonnet.md finding #3).
how_to_test: Attempt to construct a Session with risk = RiskStatus::WorkspaceChanged via test code and confirm risk_reasons surfaces 'Workspace changed'; separately confirm no live discovery flow ever produces this value (verify by code inspection / a targeted unit test on each integration's risk computation).

feature_name: RiskStatus::ConflictingMetadata is modeled but never assigned by current discovery
user_story: As a user, I expect a documented ConflictingMetadata risk category to exist for sessions with disagreeing evidence, but no current integration actually assigns this status in v0.1.0.
expected_behaviour: `RiskStatus::ConflictingMetadata` exists in the enum and `risk_reasons` surfaces `"metadata conflicts"` (src/session.rs, src/launch.rs), but no discovery path in pi/claude/codex/omp ever constructs it (documented as unreachable functionality in docs/review/round-1-sonnet.md finding #3).
how_to_test: Construct a Session with risk = RiskStatus::ConflictingMetadata via test code and confirm risk_reasons surfaces 'metadata conflicts'; confirm no live discovery flow currently produces this value.

feature_name: confirm_always forces a confirmation prompt even for a risk-free session
user_story: As a user who wants confirmation on every Resume regardless of risk, I want a synthetic 'confirmation requested' reason to appear when there is otherwise no risk.
expected_behaviour: `risk_reasons` appends `"confirmation requested"` only `if confirm_always && reasons.is_empty()` (src/launch.rs), so a normal-risk session still gets a non-empty reasons list and thus a prompt under `--confirm-always`.
how_to_test: Select a normal-risk session with `--confirm-always` set and confirm the prompt shows 'Risk: confirmation requested'.

feature_name: Confirmation prompt format: 'Resume <id> in <workspace>?' plus Risk line and y/N
user_story: As a user, I want the confirmation prompt to clearly state which session and workspace I'm about to resume, and only proceed on an explicit 'y'/'yes'.
expected_behaviour: `confirm()` writes `Resume {id:?} in {workspace}?`, then a `Risk: <reasons joined by ", ">` line if reasons are non-empty, then `Continue? [y/N] `, and only returns `Ok(true)` for trimmed lowercase input `"y"` or `"yes"` — anything else (including empty/Enter) is a refusal (src/launch.rs), tested by `refusal_is_default` (src/launch.rs).
how_to_test: At the confirmation prompt, press Enter with no input and confirm the resume is refused (exit 0, no launch); then answer 'y' and confirm the resume proceeds.

feature_name: Declining the confirmation prompt exits 0 without resuming
user_story: As a user, I want to be able to back out at the confirmation prompt without it being treated as an error.
expected_behaviour: `resume_selected` returns `EXIT_OK` on `Ok(false)` from `launch::confirm` (src/app.rs).
how_to_test: At the confirmation prompt, answer 'n' (or anything other than y/yes) and confirm the process exits 0 with no session launched.

feature_name: Revalidation blocks resume when the agent CLI has disappeared
user_story: As a user, I want resume to detect that the target agent's CLI binary is no longer installed/executable before it tries to exec it, and to fail with a clear message rather than a confusing exec error.
expected_behaviour: `revalidate` checks `command_available(&spec.program)` (searching PATH or, for a path-like program, checking executability directly) and returns `Err(RevalidationError::CliUnavailable)` -> displayed as "agent CLI is no longer available" (src/launch.rs (revalidate), (command_available)), regression-tested by `cli_disappearing_before_exec_is_rejected` which removes the CLI file between capture and revalidate (src/launch.rs).
how_to_test: Discover a session, then remove/rename the corresponding agent binary from PATH, select the session, and confirm resume refuses with 'agent CLI is no longer available' and exits EXIT_ERROR (1).

feature_name: Revalidation blocks resume when the transcript identity changed since selection
user_story: As a user, I want resume to detect if the selected session's transcript file was modified or replaced between picker selection and exec time, and refuse rather than resume stale/wrong data.
expected_behaviour: `revalidate` re-reads `FileIdentity::read(&evidence.transcript)` and compares dev/ino/len/modified against the captured `LaunchEvidence`, returning `Err(RevalidationError::TranscriptChanged)` on any mismatch (src/launch.rs (compare), (FileIdentity::read)), regression-tested by `detects_transcript_and_workspace_replacement` which rewrites the transcript file's contents post-capture (src/launch.rs).
how_to_test: Discover and select a session in the picker, then edit/overwrite the underlying transcript.jsonl file before confirming, and confirm resume refuses with 'transcript identity changed after selection'.

feature_name: Revalidation blocks resume when the Workspace directory disappeared
user_story: As a user, I want resume to detect that the Workspace directory was deleted between selection and exec, and refuse rather than exec into a missing directory.
expected_behaviour: `revalidate` returns `Err(RevalidationError::WorkspaceUnavailable)` when `FileIdentity::read(&spec.cwd)` fails (src/launch.rs).
how_to_test: Select a session, delete its recorded workspace directory before confirming, and confirm resume refuses with 'Workspace is no longer available'.

feature_name: Revalidation blocks resume when the Workspace was replaced (same path, different directory)
user_story: As a user, I want resume to detect that the workspace directory at the recorded path was replaced (e.g. removed and recreated) between selection and exec, so a stale identity isn't silently reused.
expected_behaviour: `revalidate` compares the freshly-read `FileIdentity` of `spec.cwd` against the captured `evidence.workspace_identity` and also checks `spec.cwd != evidence.workspace`, returning `Err(RevalidationError::WorkspaceChanged)` on mismatch (src/launch.rs), regression-tested by `detects_transcript_and_workspace_replacement`'s second half, which removes and recreates the workspace directory (src/launch.rs).
how_to_test: Select a session, then `rmdir` and recreate its recorded workspace directory (same path, new inode) before confirming, and confirm resume refuses with 'Workspace was replaced after selection'.

feature_name: Revalidation blocks resume for a Session whose support status is not Supported
user_story: As a user, I want resume to refuse to resume a session that isn't fully Supported (e.g. Discover Only), rather than attempting a broken launch.
expected_behaviour: `revalidate` immediately returns `Err(RevalidationError::Unsupported)` if `session.support != SupportStatus::Supported` (src/launch.rs); separately, `resume_selected` also checks support before even calling revalidate and exits EXIT_USAGE with 'selected Session is unavailable' if not Supported (src/app.rs (now routes through the unified errors::E3003 catalog — exit code unchanged at 2)).
how_to_test: Select a Discover Only session (e.g. a Claude transcript with disagreeing filename/sessionId but a recorded cwd) and confirm resume refuses cleanly rather than attempting to exec.

feature_name: Revalidation always runs before the confirmation prompt and before exec
user_story: As a user, I want stale/broken sessions caught before I'm even asked to confirm, so I never see a misleading confirmation prompt for something that can't actually be resumed.
expected_behaviour: `resume_selected` calls `launch::revalidate` immediately after the support check and before computing `risk_reasons`/calling `should_confirm` (src/app.rs (support, revalidate, risk/confirm, exec)): revalidate -> risk_reasons/confirm -> exec, in that exact order.
how_to_test: Trigger any revalidation failure condition (CLI removed, transcript changed, workspace changed/removed) and confirm no confirmation prompt is ever shown — resume fails immediately with the revalidation error.

feature_name: exec replaces the current process via native program/argv, never a shell string
user_story: As a user, I want resume to hand off to the agent CLI directly (replacing its own process image) using discrete argv, so there's no shell injection risk and no wrapper process left behind.
expected_behaviour: `launch::exec` (unix) builds `std::process::Command::new(&spec.program).args(&spec.argv).current_dir(&spec.cwd)`, sets each `spec.env` pair, and calls `.exec()` from `CommandExt`, which replaces the process image in place; if `exec()` returns at all, it is always an error, which `resume_selected` reports before returning `EXIT_ERROR` (src/launch.rs, src/app.rs).
how_to_test: Resume a session and, from a shell, confirm the resume process's PID is inherited by the launched agent CLI (e.g. via `exec` semantics, not a child process) using `ps`/`exec`-tracing tools.

feature_name: exec preserves each integration's isolation environment overrides
user_story: As a user with a nondefault agent config root (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME, PI_CONFIG_DIR) or a custom Pi/OMP session dir, I want resume's exec to preserve that override so the resumed agent looks in the same place resume did.
expected_behaviour: Each `ResumeSpec.env` is populated per-integration only when nondefault (Claude: `resume_spec` adds `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` iff `root.nondefault`, src/integration/claude/resume.rs; Codex: adds `CODEX_HOME` iff `!is_default_root(...)`, src/integration/codex/resume.rs; OMP: `resume_env` propagates `PI_CONFIG_DIR` iff `roots.config_root_overridden`, src/integration/omp/resume.rs). CORRECTED: OMP does NOT 'always' propagate PI_CONFIG_DIR (the CSV's original wording was inaccurate) — it uses the same nondefault-only discipline as Claude and Codex, propagating only when an explicit config-root override was set at discovery time; `launch::exec` applies all `spec.env` pairs before exec (src/launch.rs).
how_to_test: Set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to a nondefault path, discover and resume a Claude session, and confirm (e.g. via a fake claude CLI script that echoes env) that CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is set to the same nondefault path in the launched process.

feature_name: SUPERSEDED: `status_label` (ACTIVE/READY/DISCOVER/etc. text column) was removed; Supported+Active is now visible only via JSON `support`/`activity` fields
user_story: As a user scanning the picker, I previously relied on an ACTIVE status label; I want to know that label no longer exists so I don't look for it in --list/picker output, and instead check `--json`'s `support`/`activity` fields for the same signal.
expected_behaviour: `status_label` no longer exists anywhere in `src/app.rs` (confirmed by repo-wide grep, 0 matches) — it was removed when the row format changed to `UPDATED AGENT[PROFILE] TITLE BRANCH` (commit 3877fe1, see `picker-row-format`). A Supported+Active session is still fully distinguishable via `--json`'s `support: "Supported"` and `activity: "Active"` fields (src/app.rs `JsonSession`), just never as inline list/picker text.
how_to_test: Run `resume --json` against a Supported+Active session fixture and confirm `support`/`activity` reflect it; confirm `resume --list` shows only UPDATED/AGENT/TITLE/BRANCH with no status text.
fix_ref: src/app.rs (activity_label) + (json_session): --json now emits the bare Active/Inactive/Unknown label instead of ActivityStatus' Debug rendering, which leaked Rust struct syntax and a wall-clock time; regression test src/app.rs (json_activity_is_the_bare_label_for_every_variant)

feature_name: Supported + non-Active session is distinguishable in JSON
user_story: As a user, I previously relied on a READY status label distinguishing a resumable session with no active-use evidence; I want to know that label no longer exists in --list/picker text, and instead check `--json`'s fields.
expected_behaviour: There is no READY status text in the picker or `--list`; the row format is `UPDATED AGENT[PROFILE] TITLE BRANCH` only. A Supported, non-Active session is distinguishable through `--json`, whose `support` field reads "Supported" and whose `activity` field is not "Active". `SupportStatus` and `ActivityStatus` are the two independent enums behind those fields, per product-design.md §6 ("Active Detection is optional per integration and does not affect Supported status").
how_to_test: Run `resume --json` against a fixture with a healthy Supported session and confirm the object carries support="Supported" and an activity value other than "Active"; confirm `resume --list` prints no status word for the same session.

feature_name: Discover Only sessions are reported through the JSON support field
user_story: As a user, I previously relied on a DISCOVER status label for sessions that could not be confirmed safely resumable; I want to know that label no longer exists in --list/picker text, and instead check `--json`'s `support` field.
expected_behaviour: A session whose exact Resume cannot be guaranteed is assigned `SupportStatus::DiscoverOnly` by its integration (for example Claude's parse path when the embedded sessionId disagrees with the filename UUID). No DISCOVER text is rendered in the picker or `--list`; the state is visible through `--json`'s `support` field, and per product-design.md §2 only Supported sessions may Resume.
how_to_test: Build a Claude fixture whose embedded sessionId disagrees with its filename UUID, run `resume --json`, and confirm that session reports support="DiscoverOnly"; confirm selecting it in the picker refuses to Resume.

feature_name: SupportStatus::Unsupported is a reserved variant with no production assignment
user_story: As a user, I previously relied on an UNSUPPORTED status label; I want to know that label no longer exists in --list/picker text, and that the underlying `SupportStatus::Unsupported` variant is still never constructed by any integration in v0.1.0.
expected_behaviour: `SupportStatus::Unsupported` is modeled but never constructed by production code: the only reference outside the enum is inside `src/app.rs`'s `mod tests` (which begins). The four shipped integrations only ever assign Supported, DiscoverOnly, or Unavailable. CONTEXT.md:45 documents it as reserved for a future integration that fails validation entirely, so its absence from output is intended rather than a gap.
how_to_test: `grep -rn 'SupportStatus::Unsupported' src` and confirm every non-test hit is either the enum declaration or a match-arm pattern (`SupportStatus::Unsupported => ...`) that only formats an already-existing value; confirm no fixture can make `resume --json` emit `support: "Unsupported"`.

feature_name: A gone Workspace reads as Unavailable via JSON `support` and a scoped `--list`/picker `[Unavailable]` suffix
user_story: As a user, I want a session whose Workspace directory no longer exists to be visibly flagged in `--list`/the picker (not just in `--json`), so that I don't try to resume into a directory that's gone -- and I want that flag to appear only on the affected row, never on unrelated Sessions.
expected_behaviour: `normalize_availability` (src/app.rs) assigns `SupportStatus::Unavailable` whenever the recorded workspace directory doesn't exist, surfaced via `--json`'s `support: "Unavailable"`. `support_label` (src/app.rs) also appends a ` [Unavailable]` suffix to that Session's `--list`/picker row (alongside ` [Unsupported]`/` [DiscoverOnly]` for the other non-Supported statuses); every other row's `support` stays `Supported` and carries no suffix, so the flag is scoped to the affected Session only.
how_to_test: Delete the workspace directory of a previously discovered session, run `resume --json` and confirm `support: "Unavailable"` for it; run `resume --list` and confirm only that Session's row ends in `[Unavailable]`, and no other (still-resolvable) Session's row does.

feature_name: Activity is Unknown without positive evidence; never falsely Inactive
user_story: As a user, I want resume to avoid declaring a session Inactive when correlation evidence is absent.
expected_behaviour: Pi and Claude still receive no producer evidence and remain Unknown by default. CORRECTED: OMP now DOES receive producer evidence via `correlate_live` (src/integration/omp/activity.rs, wired at src/app.rs) and can report Active. Codex `activity_status` returns Unknown unless its shared probe snapshot confirms the exact rollout by path or device/inode (src/integration/codex/activity.rs). Core guarantee holds: the default/fallback is always Unknown, and no integration ever returns `Inactive` — only `Active` or `Unknown`.
how_to_test: Run resume --json with no live agent processes (or with RESUME_DISABLE_PROC_PROBE set) and confirm every session's activity is Unknown, never Inactive. Separately confirm a live Codex/OMP process holding an open session produces Active.

feature_name: Codex open-rollout detection is process-first and O(1) in subprocesses
user_story: As a Codex user, I want a rollout held open by a live Codex process marked Active without one subprocess per session.
expected_behaviour: src/integration/codex/activity.rs executes one fixed-argv lsof probe before discovery threads, parses records with per-PID isolation, and shares an indexed ActivitySnapshot; symlink ancestor skew is confirmed by device/inode.
how_to_test: Replay lsof field output with good and malformed PIDs; query many sessions and confirm good rows survive and the fake probe executes once.

feature_name: Resuming Active Codex prompts even under --no-confirm
user_story: As a user, I want protection from two clients writing the same live rollout.
expected_behaviour: src/launch.rs risk_reasons treats Active as risky and should_confirm cannot be bypassed by --no-confirm; plans/v0.1.0-implementation.md:362 documents this pre-existing policy.
how_to_test: Select an Active Codex session with --no-confirm and confirm the risk prompt is still shown.

feature_name: Sessions sort Active first, then by recency, unknown time last
user_story: As a user, I want currently active and then recently active sessions first.
expected_behaviour: `compare_sessions` ranks Active above Inactive above Unknown activity, then orders by last activity descending, then by stable key so the order is deterministic. product-design.md §3 requires "last activity descending, unknown time last". Both `--list`/`--json` (via `discover_all`) and the picker consume this same ordering.
how_to_test: With fixtures whose activity times differ and one whose time is unknown, run `resume --json` and confirm sessions descend by activity time with the unknown-time session last; repeat twice and confirm the order is identical.

feature_name: Non-verbose diagnostics aggregate same-category occurrences into one summed count
user_story: As a user, I want repeated diagnostics of the same category (e.g. many skipped Claude files) to render as a single 'category: N' line instead of N duplicate lines, so stderr stays readable.
expected_behaviour: `aggregate_diagnostics(errors, verbose=false)` groups purely by `category` (ignoring path/chain) via `aggregate_by(errors, |e| (e.category, None, None))`, summing counts into one entry per category (src/app.rs); `render_diagnostic` in non-verbose mode prints only `resume: <category>: <count>` (src/app.rs); this is the exact behavior added by the current HEAD commit 64e4cf2 (historical; behavior now further hardened by the M2 fix making print_diagnostics unconditional) 'fix: aggregate same-category diagnostics into one summed count in non-verbose mode', regression-tested by `non_verbose_diagnostics_collapse_by_category_summing_counts` which feeds 3 distinct-path claude_no_session_id diagnostics and 1 pi_skipped diagnostic, asserting exactly 2 collapsed lines with counts 3 and 2 (src/app.rs).
how_to_test: Craft fixtures producing 3 separate claude_no_session_id-triggering transcripts and run `resume --list` (non-verbose); confirm stderr shows exactly one line 'resume: claude_no_session_id: 3', not three separate lines.

feature_name: Verbose diagnostics preserve distinct per-path entries while merging exact duplicates
user_story: As a user diagnosing a discovery problem with --verbose, I want to see one line per distinct problematic file/path, not one blob per category, so I can find and fix the specific file.
expected_behaviour: `aggregate_diagnostics(errors, verbose=true)` groups by the full `(category, verbose_path, verbose_chain)` tuple, so distinct paths remain separate lines while exact duplicates (same category+path+chain) are merged and summed (src/app.rs), regression-tested by `verbose_diagnostics_keep_distinct_paths_but_merge_exact_duplicates`, which asserts 2 distinct paths remain separate while a true duplicate of path 'one.jsonl' is merged into a count of 2 (src/app.rs).
how_to_test: Craft fixtures producing errors on 2 distinct claude transcript paths plus one exact duplicate error, run `resume --verbose --list`, and confirm stderr shows 2 lines, with the duplicated path's line showing count 2.

feature_name: Verbose diagnostic output redacts URLs, remotes, and base64-like blobs
user_story: As a user sharing verbose diagnostic output for troubleshooting, I want URLs, git remotes, and long base64-looking blobs stripped from the path/chain text so I don't leak secrets.
expected_behaviour: `render_diagnostic` in verbose mode calls `redact_path`/`redact_text` (from `crate::diagnostics`) on `verbose_path`/`verbose_chain` before formatting the stderr line (src/app.rs); `redact_text` replaces `https://`/`http://`/`ssh://`/`git://`/`file://`/`ftp://` URLs with `[redacted-url]`, `git@host:...` remotes with `[redacted-remote]`, and 40+ char base64-alphabet runs with `[redacted-blob]` (src/diagnostics.rs), regression-tested end-to-end by `verbose_diagnostic_output_is_redacted` (src/app.rs) and at the unit level by `redact_text_removes_urls`/`redact_text_removes_git_remote`/`redact_text_removes_base64_blobs` (src/diagnostics.rs).
how_to_test: Force a diagnostic whose verbose_chain carries a `git@host:path` remote (a Claude transcript directory named `git@secret.example:api` produces one) and run `resume --verbose --list`; confirm stderr contains `[redacted-remote]` and never the literal host. A `https://` URL cannot be used here: it needs two consecutive slashes, which no single path component can contain, so no real diagnostic can carry one -- `redact_text` handles both forms through the same code path.

feature_name: Diagnostics never include session message bodies
user_story: As a user, I want diagnostic output to never accidentally echo the private content of my session transcripts.
expected_behaviour: `Diagnostic.verbose_chain` is always a short, static/derived description string set by integration code (e.g. "no embedded sessionId and no cwd; skipped"), never raw message text (src/integration/claude/discover.rs (diagnostic_chain call sites, split out of mod.rs)); `no_message_body_leaks_in_normal_mode` test explicitly asserts a chain containing 'password'/'hunter2' does not leak through normal-mode rendering, which only prints category+count (src/diagnostics.rs (no_message_body_leaks_in_normal_mode)).
how_to_test: Search all `Diagnostic {... verbose_chain: Some(...) }` construction sites across src/integration/*/mod.rs and confirm none interpolates user message text.

feature_name: --list with zero sessions found prints nothing to stdout and exits 0
user_story: As a user in a directory with no discoverable sessions, I want a clean empty result and success exit code, not an error, so scripting `resume --list | wc -l` behaves predictably.
expected_behaviour: CORRECTED: `--list` with zero sessions found does NOT print nothing — `print_list` (src/app.rs) calls `empty_list_message`, which returns `Some("No Sessions found in Scope.")` when records is empty, so stdout gets exactly that one line, not zero lines (`resume --list | wc -l` yields 1, not 0). `discovery_exit` (src/app.rs) still returns `EXIT_OK` (0) unless zero sessions AND zero successful integrations.
how_to_test: Run `resume --list` in a temp HOME with valid-but-empty agent roots and confirm stdout is exactly 'No Sessions found in Scope.' with exit 0 (unit-tested by `empty_list_has_human_readable_fallback`, src/app.rs; no end-to-end --list test currently asserts this exact stdout content — E2E gap).

feature_name: --list exits with an error only when every integration fails outright
user_story: As a user, I want resume to distinguish 'no sessions found' (success) from 'every integration failed to even run' (error), so I can tell a real problem from an empty result.
expected_behaviour: `discovery_exit` returns `EXIT_ERROR` (1) specifically when `records.is_empty() && state.successful_integrations.load(...) == 0`, i.e. zero integrations even completed successfully, not merely zero sessions found (src/app.rs); `AgentDiscovery::failed` marks `integration_ok: false` on root-resolution failure (e.g. `pi_root_unavailable`) (src/app.rs).
how_to_test: Force all four agent roots to be unresolvable (e.g. by pointing every agent env var at a location resolution can't handle) and confirm `resume --list` exits 1 with diagnostics explaining each integration's failure category.
fix_ref: src/app.rs (discover_omp): OMP returned ok even when every profile root failed to scan, so a run with no working integration still exited 0; regression test tests/step9_app.rs (omp_marks_the_integration_failed_when_every_profile_root_is_unscannable). docs/qa/run_checks.py: the check also broke the wrong directories -- an unreadable root fails is_dir() and reads as "not installed"

feature_name: One failing integration does not block sessions from the others
user_story: As a user, I want a broken/misconfigured integration (e.g. corrupted Codex root) to still let pi/claude/omp sessions come through, isolated as a diagnostic rather than aborting the whole run.
expected_behaviour: `discover_all`/`run_interactive` spawn one independent thread per agent via `discover_agent`; each thread's `AgentDiscovery` (records + errors + integration_ok) is aggregated independently into shared `DiscoveryState`/`records` (src/app.rs (discover_all), 234-308 (run_interactive)); a single agent's `AgentDiscovery::failed(category)` only contributes a diagnostic entry, never aborts other threads' results.
how_to_test: Break only the Codex integration (e.g. set CODEX_HOME to an unreadable/garbage path) while pi/claude/omp fixtures remain valid, run `resume --list`, and confirm pi/claude/omp sessions still appear alongside a codex_root_unavailable (or similar) diagnostic on stderr.
fix_ref: docs/qa/run_checks.py: harness fix only. The check chmodded ~/.codex (the root Codex probes with is_dir()) instead of ~/.codex/sessions (the directory it enumerates), so Codex looked absent rather than broken

feature_name: JSON output is exactly the v1 envelope {schemaVersion, sessions, errors}
user_story: As a tool author consuming `resume --json`, I want a stable top-level envelope with schemaVersion, sessions array, and errors array, and nothing else, so I can parse it reliably.
expected_behaviour: `JsonOutput` derives `Serialize` with fields `schema_version` (renamed `schemaVersion`, always `1`), `sessions: Vec<JsonSession>`, `errors: Vec<JsonError>` (src/app.rs); docs/json-schema.md's JSON Schema pins `required: [schemaVersion, sessions, errors]` and `additionalProperties: false` at the top level.
how_to_test: Run `resume --json 2>/dev/null` and validate the output against docs/json-schema.md's JSON Schema using any JSON Schema validator (e.g. `ajv`), confirming no additional top-level properties and schemaVersion == 1.

feature_name: JSON session objects contain exactly agent, profile, id, title, workspace, support, activity, risk
user_story: As a tool author, I want each session object in the JSON output to have a stable, complete field set with predictable null-vs-string semantics.
expected_behaviour: `JsonSession` has exactly `agent, profile, id, title, workspace, support, activity, risk` (src/app.rs); `profile`/`title`/`workspace` become JSON `null` via `Option` fields when absent; `support`/`activity`/`risk` are rendered via `format!("{:?}",...)` (Rust Debug form), explicitly documented in docs/json-schema.md as NOT lower-case enums (e.g. an Active session's activity string can embed its observed_at timestamp).
how_to_test: Run `resume --json` and confirm each session object has exactly these 8 keys, `profile`/`title`/`workspace` are `null` when unset, and `support`/`activity`/`risk` are Rust Debug-formatted strings (e.g. `"Supported"`, `"Unknown"`, `"Normal"`).

feature_name: JSON error objects contain only category and count (no verbose path/chain)
user_story: As a tool author, I want the JSON `errors` array to expose only a safe, redacted summary — never the verbose per-path diagnostic detail that stays on stderr.
expected_behaviour: `JsonError` has exactly `category: &str, count: usize` (src/app.rs); `print_json` (src/app.rs) builds `errors` from `aggregate_diagnostics(&errors_guard, false)` at src/app.rs — i.e. from the AGGREGATED diagnostics, not raw `state.errors` — before mapping to `JsonError`, so counts match the aggregated stderr rendering (this is the M5 fix; see docs/review/post-merge-review.md M5). Never includes `verbose_path`/`verbose_chain`.
how_to_test: Force a diagnostic with a sensitive verbose_path/verbose_chain, run `resume --json`, and confirm the JSON `errors` array entries contain only `category` and `count`, with no path/chain data, even with --verbose also passed.

feature_name: JSON output carries no message bodies, only a bounded title
user_story: As a user, I want `resume --json` to omit full/raw conversation transcripts while clearly warning that Session titles may contain a bounded excerpt derived from my first message.
expected_behaviour: `JsonSession` declares no `messages` field and no raw-transcript field, satisfying product-design.md §7 ("Neither table nor JSON includes user message bodies"). Its `title` may be a native title or a bounded deterministic one-line summary derived from the first human user input per §3, so conversation-derived text can appear there — truncated — without the full message array ever being emitted.
how_to_test: Run `resume --json` against a fixture whose transcript contains a long multi-line user message and confirm stdout contains no field holding the message body, and that `title` is a single truncated line.

feature_name: stdout contains exactly one JSON document; diagnostics never pollute stdout
user_story: As a user piping `resume --json` into `jq`, I want stdout to be pure JSON with all diagnostics routed to stderr instead.
expected_behaviour: `print_diagnostics` writes via `eprintln!` (src/app.rs (print_diagnostics)) and is called before `print_json`'s single `println!` of the serialized document (src/app.rs (dispatch), 814-854 (print_json)).
how_to_test: Run `resume --json 2>resume.errors | jq.` on a fixture that also produces diagnostics, and confirm `jq` parses stdout successfully with no extra lines, while resume.errors captures the diagnostics separately.

feature_name: JSON sessions array reflects the deterministic post-discovery sort, not interactive picker order
user_story: As a tool author, I want the --json sessions array to be in a stable, deterministic order across runs (same inputs), even though the interactive picker's visible order can differ while streaming.
