expected_behaviour: `discover_all` sorts collected records via `crate::session::compare_sessions` before either printer runs (src/app.rs); docs/json-schema.md explicitly notes 'This does not imply an exact global visible order in the asynchronously loaded interactive picker.'
how_to_test: Run `resume --json` twice in a row against the same unmodified fixtures and confirm the `sessions` array order is identical both times.

feature_name: Exit code 0 on success (session resumed after prompt cancel, or list/json completes, or Esc)
user_story: As a user or script author, I want exit code 0 whenever resume completed a normal, non-erroring flow — including a session listing with results, a user declining confirmation, or Esc in the picker.
expected_behaviour: `EXIT_OK = 0` (src/app.rs (EXIT_OK const)) is returned by: `discovery_exit` on a non-empty or at-least-one-successful-integration --list/--json run (src/app.rs); `PickerOutcome::Cancelled` when sessions/integrations succeeded (src/app.rs); `Ok(false)` from the confirmation prompt (src/app.rs).
how_to_test: Run `resume --list` with discoverable sessions and confirm `$?` is 0; press Esc in the interactive picker and confirm `$?` is 0; decline a confirmation prompt and confirm `$?` is 0.

feature_name: Exit code 1 on operational error (all integrations failed, revalidation failure, exec failure, preflight failure in production path)
user_story: As a script author, I want exit code 1 to mean 'something went wrong operationally' distinct from a usage mistake (2) or interrupt (130).
expected_behaviour: `EXIT_ERROR = 1` (src/app.rs (EXIT_ERROR const)) is returned by: `discovery_exit` when zero integrations succeeded and zero sessions found (src/app.rs); `resume_selected` on revalidation failure or exec failure (src/app.rs,345); `run_interactive`'s `PreflightFailed`/`InternalError` branches (src/app.rs); `PickerOutcome::Cancelled` with zero sessions and zero successful integrations (src/app.rs).
how_to_test: Force every integration to fail root resolution and run `resume --list`; separately, remove an agent's CLI from PATH after selecting its session and confirm both scenarios exit 1.

feature_name: Exit code 2 on usage errors (bad flags, config errors, missing directory, unknown agent, selected session unavailable)
user_story: As a script author, I want exit code 2 reserved for user/config mistakes I can fix by changing my invocation, distinct from operational failures.
expected_behaviour: `EXIT_USAGE = 2` (src/app.rs) is returned by: config load failure — now routed through the unified error catalog `errors::E1004.report_with(error).emit()` (src/app.rs; E1004's exit_code is 2, src/errors.rs, so the observable exit code is unchanged even though the internal mechanism moved to the four-line Report block); `effective_options` errors incl. unknown agent (src/app.rs, bare `resume: unknown agent "x"` message — E1005 is reserved-not-wired); Scope build failure incl. missing directory (src/app.rs, bare message — E3004 is reserved-not-wired); `resume_selected`'s unsupported-session-selected check (src/app.rs, now emits the four-line E3003 WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE block, exit_code 2); clap itself for malformed flags exits 2 independently.
how_to_test: Run `resume --list --agent bogus` and `resume /nonexistent` and confirm both exit 2; run `resume --config /bad/config.toml --list` where the config fails to parse and confirm exit 2.

feature_name: Exit code 130 exclusively on Ctrl-C interrupt of the interactive picker
user_story: As a script author, I want the conventional SIGINT exit code 130 reserved specifically for a hard Ctrl-C interrupt of the picker, not for Esc or ordinary errors.
expected_behaviour: `EXIT_INTERRUPT = 130` (src/app.rs (EXIT_INTERRUPT const)) is returned only by `PickerOutcome::Interrupted` in `run_interactive` (src/app.rs (Interrupted arm)), which itself is only produced by `classify` detecting `SkimKey::Ctrl('c')` as the final key (src/picker.rs (classify), (is_interrupt)).
how_to_test: Press Ctrl-C in the interactive picker and confirm `$?` is exactly 130; confirm no other code path (list/json/config errors, Esc, confirmation decline) ever produces 130.

feature_name: Pi agent root resolution: PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR overrides default ~/.pi/agent
user_story: As a Pi user with a nonstandard agent root, I want resume to honor PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR so discovery looks in the right place.
expected_behaviour: `agent_root` returns `inputs.agent_dir_env.clone()` when set, else `home.join(".pi/agent")` (src/integration/pi/roots.rs (fn agent_root); DEFAULT_AGENT_ROOT_RELATIVE const at src/integration/pi.rs).
how_to_test: Set PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR to a custom path containing pi session fixtures, run `resume --list --agent pi`, and confirm sessions from that custom root appear.

feature_name: Pi session root precedence: session-dir flag > PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR > settings.json sessionDir > default
user_story: As a Pi user with a custom session storage location, I want resume to resolve it using the same precedence Pi itself uses.
expected_behaviour: `resolve()` checks `session_dir_flag`, then `session_dir_env` (PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR), then `settings_dir(settings)` from a parsed settings.json `sessionDir` key, then falls back to `<agent_root>/sessions` (src/integration/pi/roots.rs (fn resolve, precedence chain)).
how_to_test: Set only PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR to a custom directory with pi fixtures and confirm resume discovers sessions there instead of the default `<agent-root>/sessions`; then also set settings.json sessionDir differently and confirm the env var still wins.

feature_name: Pi Resume spec is exactly `pi --session <absolute-jsonl-path>`, never --session-id
user_story: As a Pi user, I want resume's exact resume command to match Pi's own safest resume mechanism, using the transcript path rather than a possibly-ambiguous ID flag.
expected_behaviour: `ParsedSession::resume_spec` builds argv `["--session", <absolute-jsonl-path>]`, adding `["--session-dir", <root>]` only when `roots.custom_session_root` is true, and explicitly never uses `--session-id` (src/integration/pi/resume.rs; doc comment at src/integration/pi.rs).
how_to_test: Resume a pi session with a fake `pi` executable that echoes its argv and confirm it receives exactly `--session <path>` (plus `--session-dir <root>` only for a custom session root), never `--session-id`.

feature_name: Pi session title precedence: session_info.name, else summary of first human message
user_story: As a Pi user, I want the picker to show a meaningful title for each session, preferring an explicit name Pi set, falling back to a summary of what I actually typed.
expected_behaviour: `ParsedSession::title()` returns the trimmed `session_info_name` if non-empty, else `summary::summarize_texts` over `self.messages` (src/integration/pi/format.rs).
how_to_test: Discover a pi session with a `session_info.name` record and confirm the picker/--list title matches it exactly; discover another with no session_info but a first user message and confirm the title is a truncated summary of that message.

feature_name: Pi Active status requires validated stable-ID + transcript-path association; absence is Unknown, never Inactive
user_story: As a Pi user, I want resume to only claim a session is Active when it has real corroborating evidence (matching session-control ID and path), never guess based on process presence alone.
expected_behaviour: `activity_status` returns `Active { observed_at }` only if `control_evidence` is `Some` and `evidence.matches(parsed)` (session_id equality plus canonicalized transcript path equality), else `Unknown` — never `Inactive` (src/integration/pi/resume.rs (activity_status), (SessionControlEvidence + matches)).
how_to_test: Feed `activity_status` a mismatched or absent SessionControlEvidence and confirm the result is Unknown; feed a genuinely matching one and confirm Active with the evidence's observed_at.

feature_name: Pi sessions get BroadWorkspace risk when recorded cwd is $HOME or /
user_story: As a Pi user, I want a pi session recorded against my entire home directory to be flagged risky, same as other integrations.
expected_behaviour: `risk_status` (pi) delegates to `crate::scope::broad_workspace_risk` on the parsed workspace evidence (src/integration/pi/resume.rs).
how_to_test: Craft a pi session fixture whose header cwd is exactly $HOME, run `resume --list --agent pi`, and confirm it's flagged BroadWorkspace risk on selection.

feature_name: Pi discovery filters sessions by authoritative header cwd against Scope, not directory layout
user_story: As a Pi user, I want scope filtering to be based on the actual recorded working directory in each session's header, not on the (possibly encoded) directory it's stored under.
expected_behaviour: `discover()` applies `config.scope.contains(...)` against `parsed.workspace` (the header `cwd`), incrementing `outcome.out_of_scope` and skipping when out of range; directory names under the grouped session root are never reversed to infer workspace (src/integration/pi/discover.rs (discover fn, scope match; doc comment at discover.rs and src/integration/pi.rs)).
how_to_test: Place two pi session fixtures with different header cwd values under the same encoded-workspace directory (or across directories) and confirm Scope filtering follows only the header cwd values, not directory grouping.

feature_name: Claude root resolution: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR overrides default ~/.claude
user_story: As a Claude Code user with a nondefault config directory, I want resume to discover sessions from CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR when set.
expected_behaviour: `resolve_root` returns `ClaudeRoot { effective_root: PathBuf::from(explicit), nondefault: true }` when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set and non-empty, else `home.join(".claude")` with `nondefault: false` (src/integration/claude/roots.rs).
how_to_test: Set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to a custom directory with claude project fixtures and confirm `resume --list --agent claude` discovers sessions there.

feature_name: Claude identity contract: filename UUID matching embedded sessionId yields Supported
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want a session to be marked resumable only when resume can confirm its ID with high confidence (filename and embedded ID agree), never guessed.
expected_behaviour: `parse_candidate` sets `(OsString::from(embedded), SupportStatus::Supported)` only when `uuid_agrees(&filename_uuid_str, embedded)` is true (case-insensitive, brace-trimmed comparison via `normalize_uuid`) (src/integration/claude/format.rs (Supported branch); uuid_agrees/normalize_uuid at src/integration/claude/resume.rs).
how_to_test: Create a Claude transcript `<uuid>.jsonl` whose embedded `sessionId` exactly matches the filename UUID (case-insensitively) and confirm it discovers as Supported/READY.

feature_name: Claude identity disagreement: DiscoverOnly with cwd, skipped entirely without cwd
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want resume to never silently resume under a guessed ID when the filename and embedded sessionId disagree — surfaced for visibility only if there's at least a recorded cwd.
expected_behaviour: When `uuid_agrees` is false: if `parsed.cwd.is_none()`, `parse_candidate` returns `Err(diagnostic_chain("claude_identity_disagreement",...))` (fully skipped); otherwise it returns `SupportStatus::DiscoverOnly` (src/integration/claude/format.rs (skip, DiscoverOnly)).
how_to_test: Create a Claude transcript whose filename UUID and embedded sessionId disagree but which has a valid cwd; confirm it appears as DISCOVER, not resumable; then create one with the same disagreement but no cwd at all, and confirm it's skipped entirely (absent from --list/--json) with a claude_identity_disagreement diagnostic.

feature_name: Claude transcripts with no embedded sessionId: DiscoverOnly with cwd, skipped without
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want a transcript with no embedded sessionId at all to still be discoverable for diagnosis (if it at least has a cwd), but never treated as confidently resumable.
expected_behaviour: When `parsed.session_id` is `None`: if `parsed.cwd.is_none()`, returns `Err(diagnostic_chain("claude_no_session_id",...))`; otherwise uses the filename stem as the id with `SupportStatus::DiscoverOnly` (src/integration/claude/format.rs (skip, DiscoverOnly)) — this exact scenario is the one referenced by the app.rs test `non_verbose_diagnostics_collapse_by_category_summing_counts`'s `claude_no_session_id` fixture (src/app.rs).
how_to_test: Create a Claude transcript with no `sessionId` field anywhere but a valid `cwd`, confirm it shows DISCOVER status; create another with neither sessionId nor cwd, and confirm it's skipped with a claude_no_session_id diagnostic.

feature_name: Claude weak-identity diagnostic when filename isn't UUID-shaped and no sessionId exists
user_story: As a Claude Code user diagnosing discovery with --verbose, I want to know when a DiscoverOnly session's identity is especially unconfirmed (non-UUID filename, no embedded ID).
expected_behaviour: `parse_candidate` pushes a non-fatal `claude_weak_identity` diagnostic when `parsed.session_id.is_none() && !looks_like_uuid(&filename_uuid_str)` (src/integration/claude/format.rs), using an 8-4-4-4-12 hex-group UUID shape check (`looks_like_uuid`, src/integration/claude/resume.rs (looks_like_uuid)).
how_to_test: Create a Claude transcript file named something non-UUID-shaped (e.g. `notes.jsonl`) with a valid cwd and no sessionId; run `resume --verbose --list --agent claude` and confirm a claude_weak_identity diagnostic appears on stderr.

feature_name: Claude title precedence: explicit agent/display name, then AI title, then human-message summary
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want the most authoritative name Claude itself assigned to show first, falling back gracefully.
expected_behaviour: `parse_candidate` computes `title = parsed.agent_name.clone().or_else(|| parsed.ai_title.clone()).or_else(|| summary::summarize_texts(...))` (src/integration/claude/format.rs); explicitly documented as 'Resume presentation, not a claim of native picker equivalence' (module doc comment, README.md's 'Preview parsing' note).
how_to_test: Create fixtures exercising each precedence level independently (agent-name only, ai-title only, neither) and confirm the displayed title follows agent-name > ai-title > summary in each case.

feature_name: Claude Workspace comes only from event cwd, never the workspace-key directory name
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want resume to never guess my project directory from Claude's lossy, collision-prone encoded directory name.
expected_behaviour: Module doc comment states the workspace-key directory name 'is never reversed to infer Workspace'; `parse_candidate` builds `WorkspaceEvidence::Recorded { workspace: cwd,... }` strictly from `parsed.cwd` extracted from event `cwd` fields, never from `candidate.path`'s parent directory name (src/integration/claude/format.rs (WorkspaceEvidence); cwd extraction in interpret_record at format.rs).
how_to_test: Name a workspace-key directory something that doesn't decode back to any real path, but ensure the transcript's event cwd field is a real, valid path; confirm the discovered Workspace matches the event cwd, not anything derived from the directory name.

feature_name: Encoded workspace-key directories are pruned before any file is read
user_story: As a user with hundreds of Claude projects, I want out-of-scope ones skipped without opening their transcripts, so that listing stays fast.
expected_behaviour: Claude names each workspace-key directory by encoding the workspace path with leading '-'. `collect_candidates` applies the Scope prefilter to a directory only when its name starts with '-'; a non-matching one is counted in `pruned_dirs` and skipped without reading a single transcript. Directories whose names are not in that encoding are never pruned, because nothing can be inferred from them.
how_to_test: Create two workspace-key directories holding in-scope transcripts: one named with a '-'-encoded path outside the scope, one with an arbitrary non-'-' name. Confirm the encoded out-of-scope one contributes no session while the arbitrary-named one does.

feature_name: Claude discovery excludes nested subagent transcripts as independent sessions
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want only top-level session transcripts shown, not internal subagent artifacts nested under a workspace-key directory.
expected_behaviour: `collect_candidates` only enumerates direct `.jsonl` children of each workspace-key directory, explicitly not descending into nested directories like `subagents/` (src/integration/claude/discover.rs (collect_candidates, doc comment)).
how_to_test: Create a workspace-key directory containing both a top-level `<uuid>.jsonl` and a `subagents/<uuid2>.jsonl`; confirm only the top-level transcript appears in discovery, never the nested subagent one.

feature_name: Claude Resume spec is exactly `claude --resume <uuid>`, never --continue
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want resume's exact resume command to match Claude's documented resume mechanism precisely, targeting the exact session rather than the ambiguous 'continue most recent' behavior.
expected_behaviour: `resume_spec` builds argv `["--resume", session.resumable_id]`, explicitly documented as 'Never `--continue`' (src/integration/claude/resume.rs; doc comment at src/integration/claude/mod.rs and resume.rs).
how_to_test: Resume a Claude session with a fake `claude` executable that echoes argv and confirm it receives exactly `--resume <uuid>`, never `--continue`.

feature_name: Claude resume preserves a nondefault CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR via environment override
user_story: As a Claude Code user with a custom config directory, I want the resumed claude process to use the same config directory resume discovered sessions from.
expected_behaviour: `resume_spec` sets `env = vec![(CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, root.effective_root)]` only when `root.nondefault` is true, else an empty env vec (src/integration/claude/resume.rs).
how_to_test: Set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to a nondefault path, resume a discovered Claude session with a fake claude binary that dumps its environment, and confirm CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is set to the same value.

feature_name: Claude resume_spec fails cleanly when there's no recorded workspace
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want resume to refuse to build a resume command for a session with no recorded cwd, rather than guessing a working directory, and I want that failure to be visible in diagnostics, not silently discarded.
expected_behaviour: `resume_spec` returns `Err(IntegrationError::InvalidSession { diagnostic: category "claude_missing_workspace"... })` when `session.workspace.workspace()` is `None` (src/integration/claude/resume.rs). RESOLVED (was S6 from docs/review/post-merge-review.md, an open gap where `src/app.rs` called `claude::resume_spec(&session, &root).ok()` and silently discarded the diagnostic): commit 7921808 "fix: surface claude_missing_workspace diagnostic instead of discarding it (S6)" fixed this — the diagnostic is now caught and retained (src/app.rs, see the resume-spec-build call site) instead of discarded via `.ok()`.
how_to_test: Construct a Claude session fixture with no recorded cwd, select it (or run non-interactively), and confirm both the resume-spec failure AND a `claude_missing_workspace` diagnostic are visible on stderr/`--json` errors, not silently swallowed.

feature_name: Codex root resolution: CODEX_HOME overrides default ~/.codex
user_story: As a Codex user with a nondefault data root, I want resume to discover rollouts from CODEX_HOME when set.
expected_behaviour: `effective_root()` returns `PathBuf::from(value)` when `CODEX_HOME` is set and non-empty, else `home.join(".codex")` (src/integration/codex/roots.rs).
how_to_test: Set CODEX_HOME to a custom directory containing rollout fixtures and confirm `resume --list --agent codex` discovers sessions there.

feature_name: Codex scans both sessions/ (active) and archived_sessions/ (archived) roots
user_story: As a Codex user, I want resume to find both my current and archived sessions, distinguishing them internally without hiding archived ones by default.
expected_behaviour: `rollout_roots` includes both `<effective_root>/sessions` (RolloutKind::Active) and `<effective_root>/archived_sessions` (RolloutKind::Archived) when each exists (src/integration/codex/roots.rs); `discover_with_filter` sets `parsed.archived = root.kind == RolloutKind::Archived` for each (src/integration/codex/discover.rs (discover_with_filter), (discover_with_filter_enriched)).
how_to_test: Place rollout fixtures under both `sessions/` and `archived_sessions/` and confirm `resume --list --agent codex` surfaces both sets of sessions.

feature_name: Codex identity is session_meta.payload.id and Workspace is session_meta.payload.cwd, never the filename or storage directory
user_story: As a Codex user, I want resume's identity and workspace determination to be authoritative and never guessed from where the rollout file happens to live.
expected_behaviour: `parse_rollout_records` extracts `id` from `payload.get("id")` and `cwd` from `payload.get("cwd")` inside the `session_meta` record, explicitly not the unrelated `payload.session_id` nor filename nor `workspace_roots` (src/integration/codex/discover.rs (parse_rollout_records, id, cwd); doc comment src/integration/codex/mod.rs).
how_to_test: Create a rollout file whose filename bears no relation to its session_meta.payload.id, and whose directory path differs from payload.cwd; confirm the discovered session's id/workspace match the payload fields exactly, not the filename or directory.

feature_name: Codex deduplicates user messages appearing as both event_msg and response_item
user_story: As a Codex user, I want resume's title/preview summary to not double-count the same message that Codex records twice in different record shapes.
expected_behaviour: `extract_user_messages` merges `event_msg` (`payload.type == "user_message"`) and `response_item` (`role == "user"`, `payload.type == "message"`) representations, using `push_dedup`/`fingerprint` (normalized trimmed text + attachment kind fingerprint) to avoid duplicates, capped at `MAX_USER_MESSAGES` = 1024 (src/integration/codex/discover.rs (extract_user_messages), (push_dedup), (fingerprint)).
how_to_test: Craft a rollout with the same user text appearing once as an event_msg and once as a response_item; confirm the derived title/summary reflects it only once, not twice.

feature_name: Codex import metadata is exposed only as a coarse source-kind badge, never the origin path/remote
user_story: As a Codex user with imported sessions, I want to see that a session was imported and from what kind of source, but never have the origin's private path or git remote exposed by default.
expected_behaviour: `extract_import` reads only `foreign_session_import.source_kind` (or `kind`) into `ImportMeta { source_kind }`, explicitly never a path or remote (src/integration/codex/discover.rs (extract_import), ImportMeta struct at; doc comment src/integration/codex/mod.rs).
how_to_test: Craft a rollout with a `foreign_session_import` payload containing both `source_kind` and a fictitious sensitive path/remote field; confirm only source_kind ever surfaces anywhere in resume's output.

feature_name: Codex Resume spec is exactly `codex -C <workspace> resume <uuid>`
user_story: As a Codex user, I want resume's exact resume command to match Codex's documented resume-by-id mechanism, explicitly not resuming by rollout path (which Codex doesn't document).
expected_behaviour: `resume_spec` builds argv `["-C", workspace, "resume", session.resumable_id]` (src/integration/codex/resume.rs (argv)), AGENT const at mod.rs; doc comment explicitly notes 'Codex 0.146.0 does not document Resume by rollout path, so the rollout path is never used as the resume locator.'
how_to_test: Resume a Codex session with a fake `codex` executable that echoes argv and confirm it receives exactly `-C <workspace> resume <uuid>`.

feature_name: Codex resume preserves CODEX_HOME based on discovery-time provenance, not a fresh env read
user_story: As a Codex user, I want resume's env override on Resume to reflect the root that actually discovered the session, even if CODEX_HOME changes between discovery and resume.
expected_behaviour: `resume_spec` derives the override from `session.key.effective_root` (captured at discovery time), not `std::env::var_os(ENV_CODEX_HOME)` freshly, only adding it when `!is_default_root(discovered_root, default_home)` (src/integration/codex/resume.rs (is_default_root), doc comment 'The override is derived from the session's provenance...').
how_to_test: Discover a Codex session with CODEX_HOME=/custom, then unset/change CODEX_HOME before selecting and resuming it; confirm the resumed process still receives CODEX_HOME=/custom (the discovery-time root), not the changed/absent value.

feature_name: A malformed Codex rollout file produces an isolated Error entry, never aborts discovery of other rollouts
user_story: As a Codex user, I want one corrupted rollout file to be reported and skipped, not to break discovery of all my other sessions.
expected_behaviour: `discover_with_filter` wraps each file's `parse_rollout_file` result in `DiscoveredSession::Session` or `DiscoveredSession::Error { path, error }`, continuing to the next file regardless (src/integration/codex/discover.rs (DiscoveredSession enum), match arm); `discover_codex` in app.rs converts `Error` variants into diagnostics without stopping the loop (src/app.rs).
how_to_test: Place one intentionally-corrupt rollout JSONL alongside several valid ones under CODEX_HOME/sessions and confirm `resume --list --agent codex` still lists the valid sessions while reporting a codex diagnostic for the corrupt one.

feature_name: Codex SQLite enrichment is compiled out by default; a plain build never links SQLite
user_story: As a user who never wants an extra native dependency, I want resume's default build to never touch state_5.sqlite at all.
expected_behaviour: `Cargo.toml`'s `[features] default = []` means `codex-sqlite` (which gates `dep:rusqlite`) is off by default (Cargo.toml `[features]` block); the non-feature `sqlite` shim module (`src/integration/codex/mod.rs` bottom, `#[cfg(not(feature = "codex-sqlite"))]`) provides a no-op `enrich()` that always returns `SqliteOutcome::Absent`.
how_to_test: Run `cargo build --locked` (default features) and confirm the resulting binary has no dynamic/static link to sqlite (e.g. via `otool -L`/`ldd`, or by confirming `rusqlite` doesn't appear in `cargo tree`).

feature_name: Codex SQLite enrichment (feature-gated) can fill missing title and activity time, never overriding JSONL identity
user_story: As a Codex user who has enabled the codex-sqlite feature, I want richer titles/activity timestamps for sessions whose rollout JSONL alone yields no usable title, sourced from Codex's own state_5.sqlite cache.
expected_behaviour: `apply_rows` (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs (apply_rows, title enrich)) only sets `session.sqlite_title` when `session.user_messages.is_empty()` and a matching row has a non-empty title, and always treats `activity_time`/`archived` as additive/enrich-only; `derive_title` in mod.rs only falls back to `sqlite_title` when the JSONL-derived summary is `None` (src/integration/codex/discover.rs (derive_title)).
how_to_test: Build with `--features codex-sqlite`, craft a rollout with no usable user messages but a matching state_5.sqlite row with a title, and confirm the picker/--list title reflects the DB title only in that fallback case, never overriding a JSONL-derivable title.

feature_name: Codex SQLite row disagreeing on id/cwd is dropped with a diagnostic, never overrides JSONL identity
user_story: As a Codex user, I want a corrupted or stale state_5.sqlite row that disagrees with the rollout's real id/cwd to be ignored for identity purposes, with a diagnostic so I can notice the inconsistency.
expected_behaviour: `apply_rows` checks `row.id` against `session.id` and `row.cwd` against `session.cwd`; on any disagreement it pushes a `codex_sqlite_id_mismatch`/`codex_sqlite_workspace_mismatch` diagnostic and `continue`s without enriching that session (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs (id check, cwd check)).
how_to_test: Build with `--features codex-sqlite`, craft a state_5.sqlite row whose id or cwd disagrees with a matching rollout's session_meta, and confirm (a) the session's JSONL-derived identity/workspace are unaffected and (b) a mismatch diagnostic appears with --verbose.

feature_name: Codex SQLite enrichment degrades silently (Absent) when the DB file doesn't exist
user_story: As a Codex user without a state_5.sqlite file (e.g. a fresh Codex install), I want discovery to work identically to the non-enriched path with no warning noise.
expected_behaviour: `enrich()` returns `SqliteOutcome::Absent` immediately when `!db_path.is_file()` (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs); `SqliteOutcome::summary()` returns `None` for `Absent`, so no warning is surfaced (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs).
how_to_test: Build with `--features codex-sqlite`, ensure no state_5.sqlite exists under CODEX_HOME, run `resume --list --agent codex`, and confirm output is byte-for-byte identical to the same run without the feature enabled, with no enrichment-related diagnostic.

feature_name: Codex SQLite enrichment degrades to Degraded{corrupt/locked/unsupported_schema} without blocking discovery
user_story: As a Codex user whose state_5.sqlite happens to be corrupted, locked, or has an unrecognized schema, I want Codex session discovery to keep working via JSONL, with at most a coarse warning, never a crash or blocked discovery.
expected_behaviour: `enrich()` classifies `open_readonly`/`detect_schema`/`read_rows` failures into `SqliteOutcome::Degraded { category: "locked"|"corrupt"|"unreadable"|"schema_unreadable"|"unsupported_schema"|"query_failed" }`, always falling back to unmodified JSONL-derived sessions (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs); `SqliteOutcome::summary()` renders a `codex_sqlite_degraded: <category> (falling back to JSONL)` line for Degraded outcomes (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs).
how_to_test: Build with `--features codex-sqlite`, write a garbage (non-SQLite) file at state_5.sqlite's path, run `resume --list --agent codex`, and confirm Codex sessions still discover correctly from JSONL with no crash (verify the degraded summary is at least computed, even if app.rs doesn't yet surface `SqliteOutcome::summary()` as a diagnostic — check whether app.rs's discover_codex actually surfaces this summary).

feature_name: Codex SQLite is always opened read-only via a URI with mode=ro, never immutable=1 on a live DB
user_story: As a Codex user, I want resume to never risk corrupting or interfering with Codex's own concurrently-written state_5.sqlite.
expected_behaviour: `open_readonly` builds `file:<path>?mode=ro` and opens with `SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY | SQLITE_OPEN_URI | SQLITE_OPEN_NO_MUTEX`, explicitly never `immutable=1` on a live WAL DB (documented rationale at src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs (mode=ro URI, flags)); a `assert_readonly` test helper confirms a write attempt (`CREATE TABLE`) fails on the opened connection (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs (assert_readonly)).
how_to_test: Build with `--features codex-sqlite` and run the crate's own `assert_readonly`-backed test suite (`cargo test --features codex-sqlite`), or independently open the same DB file with the same URI/flags and attempt a write, confirming it's rejected.

feature_name: OMP base config root resolution: PI_CONFIG_DIR overrides default ~/.omp
user_story: As an OMP user with a nondefault base config directory, I want resume to discover sessions relative to PI_CONFIG_DIR when set.
expected_behaviour: `config_root` returns `inputs.config_dir_env.clone()` when set, else `home.join(".omp")` (src/integration/omp/roots.rs (fn config_root)).
how_to_test: Set PI_CONFIG_DIR to a custom directory containing omp agent fixtures and confirm `resume --list --agent omp` discovers sessions there.

feature_name: OMP profile selection precedence: internal profile_flag input > OMP_PROFILE > PI_PROFILE (no CLI --profile flag exists)
user_story: As an OMP user with multiple named profiles, I want resume to select the profile using the same precedence OMP itself uses, understanding that today only OMP_PROFILE/PI_PROFILE env vars are reachable — there is no `resume --profile` command-line flag.
expected_behaviour: `select_profile` checks `inputs.profile_flag`, then `inputs.omp_profile_env` (OMP_PROFILE), then `inputs.pi_profile_env` (PI_PROFILE), each requiring a non-whitespace-only value, defaulting to `ProfileSelection::Default` (src/integration/omp/roots.rs). `profile_flag` is a real, tested field on `ResolutionInputs`, but `ResolutionInputs::from_env()` always sets it to `None` (src/integration/omp/roots.rs) and `src/cli.rs` has no `--profile` argument anywhere (0 grep matches) — so in the actual `resume` binary, only the OMP_PROFILE > PI_PROFILE env-var precedence is ever reachable; `profile_flag` exists solely for internal precedence testing.
how_to_test: Run `resume --json --agent omp --profile x` and confirm clap rejects it as an unknown argument (exit 2). The env precedence is not observable through discovery -- `discover_omp` force-resolves the unprofiled default and enumerates every `profiles/<name>` directory regardless of what OMP_PROFILE/PI_PROFILE selected, so the discovered set is identical with and without them; confirm that invariance, and read the order itself off the designated `select_profile` unit tests (integration::omp::tests::roots::profile_flag_beats_omp_and_pi_profile_env and its two siblings).

feature_name: OMP discovery enumerates the default profile plus every named profile under profiles/
user_story: As an OMP user with several named profiles, I want `resume --list` to surface sessions from all of them at once, not just whichever one is currently selected by env vars.
expected_behaviour: `discover_omp` in app.rs starts with `base_roots` (default/env-selected profile) then reads `base_roots.config_root.join(PROFILES_DIR_NAME)` and resolves an additional `EffectiveRoots` for every named-profile subdirectory found, deduping by `profile` (src/app.rs (fn discover_omp, enumeration loop)).
how_to_test: Create session fixtures under both the default OMP profile and two named profiles (`profiles/work`, `profiles/personal`), run `resume --list --agent omp`, and confirm sessions from all three appear, each tagged with the correct profile in the agent[profile] display.

feature_name: Named OMP profiles deliberately ignore PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR and XDG_DATA_HOME overrides
user_story: As an OMP user, I want named-profile agent roots to always be `<config-root>/profiles/<name>/agent`, unaffected by env vars that only apply to the unprofiled default.
expected_behaviour: `agent_root` for `ProfileSelection::Named(name)` always returns `config_root.join(PROFILES_DIR_NAME).join(name).join(PROFILE_AGENT_DIR_NAME)`, explicitly bypassing the `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`/`XDG_DATA_HOME` branches that only apply to `ProfileSelection::Default` (src/integration/omp/roots.rs (fn agent_root, Named branch)), module doc comment: 'named profiles deliberately ignore it.'
how_to_test: Set PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR to some other directory while also having a named OMP profile 'work'; confirm the 'work' profile's sessions are still discovered from `<config-root>/profiles/work/agent`, unaffected by PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR.

feature_name: Default (unprofiled) OMP agent root honors PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR before its own XDG_DATA_HOME/config-root path — deliberately overlapping Pi's root
user_story: As a user who runs both Pi and OMP and has set PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR to a custom location for Pi, I want to understand that OMP's *default profile* will also read sessions from that same directory (since OMP shares Pi's session format by convention), while a *named* OMP profile stays fully isolated from it.
expected_behaviour: `agent_root`'s `ProfileSelection::Default` arm checks `inputs.agent_dir_env` (`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) first and returns it directly if set, falling back to `XDG_DATA_HOME` then `<config-root>/agent` only when unset (src/integration/omp/roots.rs (fn agent_root, Default branch)); module doc explicitly states this is intentional (src/integration/omp/mod.rs: '`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` overrides only the unprofiled agent root'). Distinct from `omp-named-profile-ignores-pi-coding-agent-dir`, which covers the opposite (named-profile isolation) case.
how_to_test: Set PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR to a directory containing only Pi fixtures (no dedicated OMP fixture); run `resume --json --agent omp` with no profile selected and confirm the reported OMP session's id/title match the Pi fixture's content, not any separate `<config-root>/agent` fixture, because the unprofiled OMP root resolved to the same directory as Pi's.

feature_name: OMP parses a title sidecar record that may precede the v3 session header, without assuming header position
user_story: As an OMP user, I want resume to correctly read my session's title even though OMP writes a padded title record before the actual session header, unlike Pi's header-first assumption.
expected_behaviour: `find_session_header` scans all records for `type == "session"` rather than assuming position 0 (src/integration/omp/format.rs (find_session_header), module doc 'we must not reuse Pi's header-position assumptions'); `extract_session` processes `type == "title"` sidecar records via `TitleState::set` regardless of their position relative to the header (src/integration/omp/mod.rs (extract_session)).

feature_name: OMP Active status requires a genuine two-stage positive-evidence pipeline with a real staleness gate (M3 fix)
user_story: As an OMP user, I want resume to only claim Active when it has strong, multi-signal evidence (not just a leftover breadcrumb file from a closed terminal).
expected_behaviour: OMP Active is a two-stage positive-evidence pipeline. Stage 1 (`correlate_live_with`, src/integration/omp/activity.rs): for each terminal breadcrumb it requires (a) a live OMP process on that TTY via `ProcessTable::live_on_tty`, (b) a breadcrumb `recorded_at` (file mtime), and (c) a FRESHNESS GATE — `fresh = recorded_at >= process.started_at` when the process start time is known (activity.rs); when `started_at` is unavailable it falls back to a 12h window (`now - recorded_at <= BREADCRUMB_FRESHNESS`) AND emits an `OMP_BREADCRUMB_START_TIME_UNAVAILABLE` diagnostic so the unknown is visible, never silent. A breadcrumb older than the recycled-TTY process, or older than 12h with no start time, is REJECTED before any evidence is recorded. Stage 2 (`activity_status`/`ActivityEvidence::matches`, activity.rs): only evidence produced by stage 1 (live_process=true, tty=Some, breadcrumb_alive=true, matching canonical session path) maps to Active; everything else is Unknown. A stale breadcrumb alone can NEVER reach Active because stage 1 never emits evidence for it.
how_to_test: Feed `correlate_live_with` a breadcrumb whose `recorded_at` is older than the live process `started_at` and assert the evidence map is empty (`correlate_live_rejects_breadcrumb_older_than_recycled_tty_process`, src/integration/omp/tests/activity.rs). Feed a process with `started_at=None` and a breadcrumb just inside/exactly at the 12h `BREADCRUMB_FRESHNESS` boundary and assert Active + one `OMP_BREADCRUMB_START_TIME_UNAVAILABLE` diagnostic; push `recorded_at` 1s past the boundary and assert empty (`missing_process_start_time_uses_twelve_hour_freshness_fallback`, activity.rs). Also assert full positive evidence -> Active and any single missing signal -> Unknown (`correlate_live_requires_process_tty_breadcrumb_and_existing_transcript`; `activity_active_only_with_live_process_tty_and_matching_breadcrumb`).

E1002 (CONFLICTING_DIRECTION) is now wired: `Cli::direction_conflict()` is checked explicitly in `main()` before `Cli::validate()` or any clap-level conflict runs, and emits the real four-line E1002 block (src/cli.rs, src/main.rs) -- no declarative `conflicts_with` is used for --up/--down. E1001 (INVALID_SINCE) and E1003 (INVALID_DISTANCE) remain wired only as the parser-hint STRING (via `.parser_message()`), wrapped in clap's own value-parse error format -- the four-line block is intentionally not emitted for these, matching their documented `--man` "Message:" field, which is a separate, correct-as-documented design (not a gap). E1004 (INVALID_CONFIG) is wired via the four-line block (app.rs). `--confirm-always`/`--no-confirm` still conflict via a plain declarative clap `conflicts_with` with no E-code (unchanged; it has no catalog entry).
how_to_test: `resume --up 1 --down 2` (exit 2, the E1002 four-line block); `resume --since yesterday` (exit 2, message contains the E1001 parser-hint string, no four-line block); `resume --up -1` (exit 2, E1003 hint string, no four-line block); `resume --config /bad.toml --list` (exit 2, four-line E1004 block); `resume --list --confirm-always --no-confirm` (exit 2, clap ArgumentConflict plain text, no E-code).

feature_name: Streaming JSONL reader enforces line/file/record/nesting bounds to prevent unbounded allocation
user_story: As a user, I want resume reading a maliciously-crafted or actively-growing huge session file to abort bounded, never hang or OOM.
expected_behaviour: `preview::jsonl::Bounds` (DEFAULT_MAX_LINE_BYTES=8MiB, DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_BYTES=512MiB, DEFAULT_MAX_RECORDS=1M, DEFAULT_MAX_NESTING=64) is enforced in `read_buffered` (src/preview/jsonl.rs): oversized lines are counted and skipped (oversized_lines), a file exceeding the byte bound yields `FileOutcome::BoundExceeded`, the record cap stops enumeration early, and `parse_bounded` rejects JSON nesting deeper than max_nesting.
how_to_test: Craft a fixture with a >8MiB single line and a >512MiB file; confirm read_file returns BoundExceeded and the oversized_lines count, without panicking or exhausting memory.

feature_name: OMP Active detection staleness gate closes the recycled-TTY false-positive (M3 fix)
user_story: As an OMP user, I want resume to never falsely report a session Active just because a leftover terminal breadcrumb names its path while a DIFFERENT, newer process now owns that recycled TTY — a stale breadcrumb must be rejected against the live process's actual start time.
expected_behaviour: `correlate_live_with` (src/integration/omp/activity.rs) reads each breadcrumb's `recorded_at` (file mtime) and the live process's `started_at` (ProcEntry.started_at, src/proc.rs). It rejects the breadcrumb unless fresh: when `started_at` is known, `recorded_at >= started_at` (activity.rs) — so a breadcrumb written by a PREVIOUS process on that TTY, older than the current process, is dropped. When `started_at` is unavailable it falls back to a 12h `BREADCRUMB_FRESHNESS` window and emits an `OMP_BREADCRUMB_START_TIME_UNAVAILABLE` diagnostic (errors::category::OMP_BREADCRUMB_START_TIME_UNAVAILABLE) so the unknown is surfaced rather than silently trusted. This replaced the pre-fix gate, which was a tautology/no-op: it only checked a `breadcrumb_alive` boolean set without any time comparison, so any recycled-TTY breadcrumb with a live process and matching path falsely reported Active.
how_to_test: Regression test `correlate_live_rejects_breadcrumb_older_than_recycled_tty_process` (src/integration/omp/tests/activity.rs): breadcrumb recorded_at = EPOCH, process started_at = EPOCH+1s -> evidence map empty (the exploit is closed). Regression test `missing_process_start_time_uses_twelve_hour_freshness_fallback` (activity.rs): started_at=None, breadcrumb at exactly BREADCRUMB_FRESHNESS ago -> Active + 1 diagnostic; 1s older -> empty.

feature_name: OMP breadcrumb (terminal-sessions) directory resolution honors XDG_STATE_HOME for native default roots, else falls back to the agent root
user_story: As an OMP user whose install splits state under XDG_STATE_HOME, I want resume to read terminal breadcrumbs from the same place OMP writes them, so Active detection works without misreading the agent root.
expected_behaviour: `breadcrumb_directory` (src/integration/omp/activity.rs) uses `XDG_STATE_HOME/omp/terminal-sessions` for the default profile ONLY when (a) PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR is not overridden and (b) the XDG path exists as a directory; for a named profile it requires the exact `XDG_STATE_HOME/omp/profiles/<name>` path. Otherwise it falls back to `roots.agent_root/terminal-sessions`. A path-like TTY filename is rejected by the real reader (activity.rs).
how_to_test: See regression tests below.

feature_name: Codex activity process-probe honors RESUME_DISABLE_PROC_PROBE and short-circuits before any lsof/proc scan (M1 fix)
user_story: As a user in a restricted environment or running resume under a debugger/CI, I want to fully disable the lsof/proc subprocess probe so resume never spawns an external process for Codex activity detection.
expected_behaviour: `probe()` (src/integration/codex/activity.rs) calls `crate::proc::proc_probe_disabled(std::env::var_os(crate::proc::DISABLE_PROC_PROBE_ENV))` (env name `RESUME_DISABLE_PROC_PROBE`, src/proc.rs) and returns an empty ActivitySnapshot with no diagnostics before touching lsof; absent evidence leaves activity Unknown (never Inactive).
how_to_test: Set RESUME_DISABLE_PROC_PROBE=1, place a fake lsof on PATH that writes a marker file, run `resume --json --agent codex`, and confirm the marker is never created and every Codex session reports activity Unknown.

feature_name: Codex discovery emits a codex_root_unavailable diagnostic for an unreadable (permission-denied) sessions root while silently skipping a merely-absent one (M4 fix)
user_story: As a user whose ~/.codex/sessions is unreadable (e.g. wrong ownership/permissions), I want resume to surface a visible diagnostic rather than silently reporting zero Codex sessions, while a fresh install with no sessions dir at all stays quiet.
expected_behaviour: `unreadable_root` (src/integration/codex/discover.rs) distinguishes `ErrorKind::NotFound` (returns None, no error — Codex may not have created the dir) from any other read_dir failure such as permission denied (returns `IntegrationError::Io{ diagnostic{ category:"codex_root_unavailable",... } }`), surfaced via DiscoveredSession::Error in both discover_with_filter and discover_with_filter_enriched.
how_to_test: On Unix, chmod 000 a populated ~/.codex/sessions (as non-root), run `resume --json --agent codex`, and confirm exit 1 with a codex_root_unavailable entry in JSON errors; separately confirm a missing sessions dir produces no error.

feature_name: Claude discovery emits claude_root_unavailable diagnostic on permission errors reading projects/ (M4 fix)
user_story: As a Claude Code user diagnosing why no sessions appear, I want a diagnostic when the projects/ directory exists but is unreadable (permission denied), distinguishing it from a simple missing directory.
expected_behaviour: `collect_candidates` matches `io::ErrorKind::NotFound` (returns empty, no error) vs other errors (emits Diagnostic category `claude_root_unavailable`); `discover_claude` in app.rs surfaces this category and fails the integration (src/integration/claude/discover.rs, src/app.rs).
how_to_test: chmod 000 the projects/ directory under a Claude config root; run `resume --list --agent claude`; confirm a claude_root_unavailable diagnostic appears and discovery reports failure.

feature_name: M2 fix: non-verbose --list/--json print discovery diagnostics to stderr unconditionally
user_story: As a user running resume --list without --verbose, I want discovery diagnostics to still appear on stderr so I can see why sessions are missing without having to re-run with --verbose.
expected_behaviour: `run()` calls `print_diagnostics(&state, options.verbose)` UNCONDITIONALLY in both the --json branch (src/app.rs) and the --list branch (src/app.rs) — the `verbose` flag only controls whether path/chain detail is included in each rendered line, never whether diagnostics print at all. Pre-fix, the packaging branch had moved this call inside an `if options.verbose` guard, silently dropping every non-verbose diagnostic (codex_root_unavailable, omp_discovery_failed, pi_skipped, git_scope_discovery_failed, etc.).
how_to_test: Run `resume --list` (no --verbose) on a fixture producing a codex_invalid_session diagnostic; confirm stderr contains 'codex_invalid_session: N'.

feature_name: M5 fix: --json errors[] counts are aggregated (collapsed by category), matching stderr
user_story: As a tool author consuming resume --json, I want the errors[] array to expose one aggregated entry per category with a summed count, not N raw per-occurrence entries, so counts are stable and match stderr.
expected_behaviour: `print_json` (src/app.rs) calls `aggregate_diagnostics(&errors_guard, false)` at src/app.rs BEFORE constructing the `JsonError` list — collapsing same-category occurrences into one entry with a summed count, the same function `print_diagnostics` uses for stderr. Pre-fix, `print_json` iterated `state.errors` raw, so three malformed transcripts in the same category produced three duplicate-keyed JSON entries instead of one aggregated entry.
how_to_test: Force 3 same-category diagnostics (e.g. 3 corrupt codex transcripts), run `resume --json --agent codex`; confirm errors[] has ONE entry with count 3, and that count equals the stderr 'category: 3' line for the same run.

feature_name: Selecting a non-Supported Session now emits the unified four-line E3003 WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE block (exit code unchanged at 2)
user_story: As a user who selects a session resume cannot safely resume, I want a consistent, actionable four-line error explaining why, not a bare one-line message.
expected_behaviour: `resume_selected`'s support guard (src/app.rs) now calls `crate::errors::E3003.report(...).emit()` instead of a bare `EXIT_USAGE` return. `E3003` (WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE, src/errors.rs) has `exit_code: 2` — identical to the old EXIT_USAGE constant — so the user-observable exit code is UNCHANGED; only the internal mechanism and stderr formatting moved to the unified four-line catalog block.
how_to_test: Select a DiscoverOnly or Unavailable session via the picker (or construct one directly) and confirm the four-line ERROR [E3003] WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE block prints to stderr with exit code 2.

feature_name: TITLE/WORKSPACE column budget adapts to terminal width (16-60 cols, default 48 with no TTY)
user_story: As a user piping resume --list output through a script or redirecting to a file, I want the title column width to be stable regardless of terminal state, per docs/product-design.md's documented bounds.
expected_behaviour: `title_column_width` (src/app.rs) clamps the computed width to [TITLE_WIDTH_MIN=16, TITLE_WIDTH_MAX=60] and falls back to TITLE_WIDTH_DEFAULT (48) when there is no controlling terminal (the common case for --list/--json in tests, CI, and redirected/piped invocations).
how_to_test: Run `resume --list` with no controlling terminal (e.g. in CI or with output redirected) and confirm the title column is exactly the documented default width.

feature_name: PreviewPosition::Auto picks right (wide terminal) vs bottom (narrow terminal)
user_story: As a user without an explicit preview_position preference, I want resume to automatically choose a sensible preview layout based on my terminal width.
expected_behaviour: `build_production_options` (src/picker.rs) maps PreviewPosition::Auto to "right" when `tty_size()` width >= 100, else "down" (bottom); Right/Bottom map directly without the width check.
how_to_test: In a wide terminal (>=100 cols) with preview_position=auto, confirm the preview renders on the right; in a narrower terminal, confirm it renders at the bottom.

feature_name: Pi discovery parses v1, v2, and v3 session headers identically
user_story: As a Pi user with older session files, I want resume to discover sessions regardless of which Pi header version produced them.
expected_behaviour: `extract_session` finds the first record with `type=="session"` and extracts id/cwd/parentSession/timestamp regardless of the version field; v1/v2/v3 are field-compatible (src/integration/pi/discover.rs, find_session_header at).
how_to_test: Write three fixtures with type="session" headers tagged version 1, 2, and 3 respectively (same id/cwd); confirm all three discover successfully.

feature_name: Pi activity_time uses message timestamps, then header, then file mtime
user_story: As a Pi user, I want session recency to reflect real activity, falling back gracefully when timestamps are sparse.
expected_behaviour: ParsedSession.activity_time = latest_message_time.or(header_time).or(file_mtime) (src/integration/pi/discover.rs).
how_to_test: Write a session with user-message timestamps newer than the header; confirm activity_time follows the message. Write one with only a header timestamp; confirm it follows the header. Write one with no timestamps; confirm it falls back to file mtime.

feature_name: Pi discovery dedupes sessions by canonical transcript path under the effective session root
user_story: As a Pi user with symlinked or aliased session files, I want resume to show each real session only once.
expected_behaviour: discover() canonicalizes each jsonl_path and dedupes by (session_root, canonical_path); the same id under different roots yields distinct sessions (src/integration/pi/discover.rs).
how_to_test: Create two symlinks to the same transcript under the same session root; confirm only one session appears. Create the same id under two different session roots; confirm both appear as distinct.

feature_name: Pi discovery tolerates malformed middle records and truncated tails without aborting
user_story: As a Pi user with a partially-corrupt session file, I want resume to salvage valid records rather than skipping the whole file.
expected_behaviour: The shared jsonl reader skips malformed middle records (counted in read.malformed_middle) and marks incomplete tails as IncompleteTail; extract_session retains all valid records parsed before the corruption (src/integration/pi/discover.rs).
how_to_test: Write a session jsonl with a valid header, a malformed JSON line in the middle, and a valid user message after it; confirm the session still discovers with the valid message.

feature_name: Claude user-message extraction excludes tool_result blocks and injected (isMeta/isSidechain) records from the title summary
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want session titles to reflect what I actually typed, not tool output or agent-injected sidechain content.
expected_behaviour: interpret_record only treats type="user" records with non-tool_result content and !isMeta/!isSidechain as human input (src/integration/claude/format.rs, has_human_input, is_injected).
how_to_test: Write a transcript with a user record containing only tool_result blocks; confirm it does not contribute to the title. Write one with isMeta=true; confirm it is excluded.

feature_name: Claude discovery never modifies any file, directory, or mtime
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want resume's discovery to be purely read-only so it cannot corrupt my session store.
expected_behaviour: discover() and collect_candidates only read directories and open files for reading; no file is opened for write, no directory entry or mtime is changed (src/integration/claude/discover.rs doc comment).
how_to_test: Snapshot all file mtimes and contents under a Claude config root before and after `resume --list --agent claude`; confirm zero changes.

feature_name: Claude discovery emits claude_truncated, claude_oversized, and claude_malformed non-fatal diagnostics while retaining valid sessions
user_story: As a Claude Code user diagnosing with --verbose, I want to know when a transcript was truncated, oversized, or had malformed middle records, without losing the session entirely.
expected_behaviour: parse_candidate pushes nonfatal diagnostics for IncompleteTail (claude_truncated), BoundExceeded (claude_oversized), and malformed_middle > 0 (claude_malformed), but still returns Some(session) (src/integration/claude/format.rs).
how_to_test: Write a transcript ending mid-JSON-line; confirm claude_truncated appears and the session is retained. Write one exceeding the read bound; confirm claude_oversized. Write one with a malformed middle line; confirm claude_malformed.

feature_name: Git common-dir lookup is memoized per canonical Workspace (performance contract)
user_story: As a user resuming inside a large repo with many sessions, I want resume to query each Workspace's git common directory at most once, so discovery stays fast rather than spawning one git subprocess per session.
expected_behaviour: In ScopeMode::Git, Scope::contains_workspace resolves git_common_dir via cached_git_common_dir (src/scope.rs), keyed by canonical path, shared via Arc<Scope> across per-agent threads. Non-Git modes skip the spawn entirely (src/scope.rs).
how_to_test: Run contains_workspace against the same canonical path repeatedly and confirm only the first call spawns git.

feature_name: A Session whose Workspace was deleted is still Scope-matched via its last-known real path
user_story: As a user, I want a session recorded under a now-deleted directory to still be matched by Scope (so it appears, marked Unavailable) rather than silently vanishing from the list.
expected_behaviour: resolve_missing_workspace_path (src/scope.rs) canonicalizes the nearest existing ancestor and re-appends the missing suffix; contains_workspace falls back to it when canonicalize fails (src/scope.rs).
how_to_test: Discover a session under /real/base/deleted (base exists, deleted subdir does not); confirm it is still matched under --down all, while an unrelated /other/deleted path is not.

feature_name: Config parse errors report file path, line/column, and offending field
user_story: As a user with a typo in config.toml, I want the error to name the file, line, and field so I can fix it without guessing.
expected_behaviour: ConfigError::Parse interpolates {source} (the toml::de::Error Display carrying line/column + field) alongside {path:?} (src/config.rs), so the message includes 'line 1' and the field name.
how_to_test: Write config.toml containing `mystery = true`; run `resume --config <path> --list`; confirm the error contains 'line 1' and 'mystery'.

feature_name: Interactive picker waits for Pi/OMP/Claude before opening; Codex discovers in the background
user_story: As a user with many discovered sessions, I want a single, stable, correctly-sorted view without waiting on whichever agent happens to be slowest -- observed on a real corpus: Pi/OMP/Claude finish in well under 200ms, Codex can take 18+ seconds.
expected_behaviour: `run_interactive` splits configured agents into sync (everything but Codex) and, when at least one other agent is also configured, async (Codex alone). Sync agent threads are joined as before (one `resume: <agent> scanned (<elapsed>)` progress line per agent to stderr, in real completion order) before the Picker opens. Codex's thread is spawned but never joined before opening the Picker; it merges its records into the same `Arc<Mutex<Vec<PickerCandidate>>>` the Picker reads (`merge_records`) whenever it finishes, and its own progress line is buffered and printed only after the Picker returns (never mid-render, since Skim owns the terminal). `picker::run_tabbed_picker` takes an optional `BackgroundAgent { label, pending }` and shows a `(codex still scanning)` header hint while it runs. When Codex is the only configured agent it stays synchronous (src/app.rs run_interactive, merge_records; src/picker.rs run_tabbed_picker, BackgroundAgent).
how_to_test: Run `resume` from a real Scope where Codex's corpus is large; observe the Picker opens within ~1s showing Pi/OMP/Claude's Sessions and a `(codex still scanning)` header hint, well before Codex would traditionally finish. After Codex finishes, switch tabs (Alt+Left/Alt+Right) and confirm a `codex` tab appears with its Sessions and the hint clears. Exit (Esc) and confirm `resume: codex scanned (<elapsed>)` prints after the Picker's screen is gone, with a clean (non-corrupted) render throughout.

feature_name: Picker presents an All tab plus one tab per agent; Alt+P/Alt+N page, Alt+Left/Alt+Right switch tabs
user_story: As a user, I want to browse all sessions together (All) or narrow to one agent (a per-agent tab), and within either view page through more than 50 sessions, using simple keys.
expected_behaviour: `run_tabbed_picker` builds tabs as `All` (index 0) plus one tab per distinct `PickerCandidate.agent`, in first-seen order after the global ascending sort; each tab is independently paginated at `PAGE_SIZE` (50), defaulting to its newest page. `Alt+P`/`Alt+N` (`classify_nav`, `SkimKey::Alt('p')`/`Alt('n')`) move pages within the current tab, only bound when that direction exists. `Alt+Left`/`Alt+Right` (`SkimKey::AltLeft`/`AltRight`) cycle tabs with wraparound and reset to the target tab's newest page. Every page turn or tab switch relaunches a small, fresh Skim instance over just that slice (src/picker.rs run_tabbed_picker, run_single_view, build_tabbed_options, classify_nav).
how_to_test: With 3+ agents and one agent having 50+ sessions: from the All tab's last page, press Alt+P and confirm the header reads a lower page number and the newest-page-only session disappears; press Alt+Left/Alt+Right and confirm the header's bracketed tab name changes and cycling wraps past the last tab back to All; confirm Enter still resolves the correct session from whichever tab/page is active.

feature_name: Codex discovery uses up to 8 bounded worker threads instead of scanning one file at a time
user_story: As a user with a large Codex rollout store, I want discovery to finish quickly even on a corpus much bigger than my current Scope, since Codex's store has no per-directory Workspace pruning to shrink the file list before reading.
expected_behaviour: discover_with_filter_enriched splits each root's file list across up to MAX_DISCOVERY_WORKERS=8 scoped threads (parallel_map; falls back to sequential below PARALLEL_THRESHOLD=16 files to avoid thread-spawn overhead on small corpora), reassembling results in original sorted order before any downstream code (filter, sqlite enrichment, Session construction) sees them -- output is unaffected by the parallelism, only wall-clock time (src/integration/codex/discover.rs parallel_map, discover_with_filter_enriched).
how_to_test: Time `resume --agent codex --json <dir>` against a real large Codex corpus (hundreds+ rollouts) with a cold cache; observe wall time close to `user+sys` CPU time divided across cores rather than serial. Compare stdout against a small-corpus (<16 files, forces the sequential fallback) run for parity.

feature_name: Codex discovery cache: reuse an unchanged rollout's parsed content across runs
user_story: As a user who runs resume repeatedly against the same machine's Codex sessions (often from different project directories over time), I want repeat invocations to skip re-reading and re-parsing rollout files that have not changed.
expected_behaviour: codex::cache::DiscoveryCache loads a JSON file at $XDG_CACHE_HOME/resume/codex-discovery-v1.json (falling back to ~/.cache/resume/; codex::cache::cache_path) keyed by each rollout's canonical absolute path, storing (size, mtime, parsed-content-or-no-session). A lookup hit (matching size+mtime) skips the file read and JSON parse entirely; a miss does a full, ungated parse (bypassing the Scope Workspace-gate, since a gate rejection is Scope-specific and must never be cached as a durable 'no session' fact) and records the result. The cache is purely non-authoritative: a missing/corrupt/version-mismatched file loads as empty (never an error), a write failure is silently swallowed, and deleting the file is always safe -- the rollout JSONL remains the source of truth. SQLite enrichment hints are never cached; they are recomputed fresh on every run on top of the cached-or-parsed content (src/integration/codex/cache.rs; src/integration/codex/discover.rs parse_for_discovery) On save, an entry whose path falls under the current run's effective_root but was not observed this run (the file no longer exists) is pruned as an orphan -- dynamic, run-driven garbage collection with no separate sweep job, since caching guarantees every currently-existing file under that root is always seen. An entry under a *different* effective_root (a different CODEX_HOME from an earlier run) is never pruned, since this run has no evidence about a root it did not scan (DiscoveryCache::save).
how_to_test: Run `resume --agent codex --json <dir>` twice against the same real Scope with the same $XDG_CACHE_HOME; diff the two JSON outputs (must be byte-identical) and observe the second run is dramatically faster. Modify a rollout file's content and confirm its cached entry is invalidated (next run re-parses it). Delete the cache file and confirm the next run degrades gracefully to a full fresh scan with identical output Delete a rollout file between two runs against the same CODEX_HOME/XDG_CACHE_HOME and confirm its cache entry is gone after the second run's save; confirm an entry cached under a *different* CODEX_HOME in an earlier run survives untouched.

feature_name: OpenCode root honours XDG_DATA_HOME
user_story: As a user with a relocated XDG data directory, I want resume to find my OpenCode sessions where OpenCode actually stores them, so that relocation does not silently hide my history.
expected_behaviour: `roots::effective_root` returns `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode` when XDG_DATA_HOME is set and non-empty, otherwise `~/.local/share/opencode`. An empty XDG_DATA_HOME is treated as unset, not as a relative root.
how_to_test: Point XDG_DATA_HOME at a fixture directory holding `opencode/opencode.db`, run `resume --json -a opencode`, and confirm its sessions appear; repeat with XDG_DATA_HOME set to the empty string and confirm the HOME fallback is used instead.

feature_name: Only opencode.db is read; legacy JSON storage is ignored
user_story: As a user upgrading from a pre-1.0 OpenCode install, I want resume to report the sessions OpenCode itself would resume, so that stale JSON files do not resurrect dead sessions.
expected_behaviour: Sessions come exclusively from the `session` table of `opencode.db` (`roots::DB_FILENAME`). A leftover `storage/session/*.json` or `storage/project/*.json` tree is never read, because current OpenCode no longer writes it.
how_to_test: Create a fixture root containing both `opencode.db` with one session and a `storage/session/legacy.json`; run `resume --json -a opencode` and confirm only the database session is listed.

feature_name: The OpenCode database is opened strictly read-only
user_story: As a user with OpenCode running, I want resume never to modify or lock my session database, so that browsing sessions cannot corrupt or block the live agent.
expected_behaviour: `open_readonly` opens the database with `SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY | SQLITE_OPEN_NO_MUTEX` and a bounded busy timeout, so a concurrently-writing OpenCode is never blocked and the file is never mutated. This matches the read-only posture the product requires of every integration.
how_to_test: With a fixture `opencode.db`, record the file's mtime and size, run `resume --json -a opencode`, and confirm both are unchanged and no `-wal`/`-journal` file was created.

feature_name: A database without a session table degrades to a diagnostic
user_story: As a user whose OpenCode database predates or postdates the expected schema, I want a clear diagnostic instead of a crash, so that one integration cannot take down the whole listing.
expected_behaviour: Discovery pre-checks that the `session` table exists before querying. A database missing that table yields no Sessions and a diagnostic rather than a SQL error surfaced to the user, and never aborts the other integrations.
how_to_test: Create an `opencode.db` containing an unrelated table only, run `resume --json --verbose`, and confirm exit code 0, zero opencode sessions, and a diagnostic on stderr.

feature_name: A missing OpenCode database reports opencode_root_unavailable
user_story: As a user who has never run OpenCode, I want resume to say so rather than fail, so that a missing agent is normal rather than an error.
expected_behaviour: When `opencode::discover` returns `Ok(None)` (no database at the effective root), `app::discover_opencode` records the diagnostic category `opencode_root_unavailable` and contributes zero Sessions. Exit code is unaffected.
how_to_test: Run `resume --json --verbose -a opencode` with HOME pointing at a fixture that has no `opencode` data directory; confirm exit 0, zero sessions, and `opencode_root_unavailable` on stderr.

feature_name: A build without the opencode feature yields zero OpenCode sessions
user_story: As a user of a default build, I want OpenCode to be inert rather than half-working, so that missing SQLite support never produces partial or wrong results.
expected_behaviour: `discover_stub::discover` is compiled when the `opencode` cargo feature is off. It always returns `Ok(None)` without touching the filesystem, so the binary reports zero OpenCode Sessions and never attempts a degraded scan. Other agents are unaffected.
how_to_test: Build with a plain `cargo build` (no `--features opencode`), point HOME at a fixture that does contain a populated `opencode.db`, run `resume --json --verbose -a opencode`, and confirm zero sessions and a diagnostic.

feature_name: The feature-off diagnostic category matches what the code emits
user_story: As a user reading stderr, I want the documented diagnostic name to be the one I actually see, so that I can search the docs for what my terminal printed.
expected_behaviour: README.md:154 states that `-a opencode` on a feature-off build reports `opencode_root_unavailable`, and `src/app.rs` emits exactly that. The category must be identical in docs and code so the diagnostic is greppable.
how_to_test: Build without the feature, run `resume --json --verbose -a opencode`, capture the stderr category token, and confirm it appears verbatim in README.md and in every source doc comment describing this path.
fix_ref: src/integration/opencode/discover_stub.rs (NO_SESSIONS_CATEGORY) + src/integration/opencode/discover.rs (NO_SESSIONS_CATEGORY) + src/app.rs (discover_opencode): the documented opencode_disabled category was never emitted; the Ok(None) arm now reports per build which of the two happened

feature_name: Feature-off and no-data are distinguishable to the user
user_story: As a user who built without SQLite support, I want to be told my build lacks OpenCode rather than that I have no OpenCode sessions, so that I know rebuilding would help.
expected_behaviour: A build compiled without the `opencode` feature and a build that simply has no OpenCode database both reach `AgentDiscovery::failed("opencode_root_unavailable")`. If the two cases are indistinguishable on stderr, the feature-off case is unactionable and needs a distinguishing hint.
how_to_test: Run `resume --json --verbose -a opencode` twice — once on a feature-off build against a populated fixture, once on a feature-on build against an empty fixture — and diff the stderr; they must not be byte-identical.
