feature_name: Resume launches the exact selected OpenCode session
user_story: As a user picking one of several OpenCode sessions, I want that specific session resumed, so that selection is meaningful.
expected_behaviour: `resume_spec` builds `opencode --session <id>`. `--continue`/`-c` (last session) and `--fork` are never used: the first ignores the selection and the second branches instead of resuming.
how_to_test: Put a fake `opencode` executable early on PATH that logs its argv, select an OpenCode session that is not the most recent, and confirm the logged argv is `opencode --session <that id>`.

feature_name: OpenCode is launched with cwd set to the recorded workspace
user_story: As a user resuming a session recorded in another directory, I want OpenCode to start in that directory, so that its own working-directory detection agrees with the session.
expected_behaviour: The resume spec sets the child process cwd to `session.directory`, the absolute path OpenCode recorded at session creation, rather than inheriting the terminal's current directory.
how_to_test: With the argv-logging fake `opencode` on PATH, also log `pwd`; resume a session whose recorded directory differs from the shell's cwd and confirm the logged pwd is the recorded directory.

feature_name: OpenCode sessions carry no profile segment
user_story: As a user reading the picker rows, I want the AGENT[PROFILE] column to omit a profile for OpenCode, so that it does not imply an isolation concept OpenCode lacks.
expected_behaviour: OpenCode has no profile or isolation concept, so `SessionKey::profile` is always `None` for its Sessions and the row renders as a bare agent name with no bracketed profile.
how_to_test: Run `resume --json -a opencode` against the fixture and confirm every object's profile field is null; confirm `resume --list` shows `opencode` with no `[...]` suffix.

feature_name: `-a opencode` restricts discovery to OpenCode
user_story: As a user with several agents installed, I want to list only OpenCode sessions, so that I can narrow a crowded picker.
expected_behaviour: `opencode` is a member of `cli::SUPPORTED_AGENTS`, so `--agent opencode` is accepted by CLI validation and restricts discovery to that one integration.
how_to_test: Run `resume --json -a opencode` against a fixture holding sessions for several agents and confirm every returned object has agent `opencode`.

feature_name: First run prompts for the agents to scan
user_story: As a new user, I want to choose which agents resume scans on first run, so that I am not forced to wait on agents I do not use.
expected_behaviour: With no `~/.resume/settings.json` present, `load_or_setup` calls `run_setup`, which prints a numbered list of `SUPPORTED_AGENTS` and reads one selection line from the controlling terminal.
how_to_test: With an isolated HOME containing no `.resume/settings.json`, run `resume` under a PTY and confirm the numbered agent list and the `Selection (for example 1,3; `all`; or `none`): ` prompt appear before any discovery output.

feature_name: Setup accepts comma-separated 1-based agent numbers
user_story: As a user choosing a subset of agents, I want to type their numbers, so that selection is quick and unambiguous.
expected_behaviour: `parse_selection` maps each comma-separated token to a 1-based index into `SUPPORTED_AGENTS`, ignores surrounding whitespace, and de-duplicates repeats while preserving `SUPPORTED_AGENTS` identity (so `2, 1, 2` selects two distinct agents).
how_to_test: Run setup under a PTY, answer `2, 1, 2`, and confirm the written settings.json lists exactly two agents and no duplicates.

feature_name: Setup accepts `all` and `none` case-insensitively
user_story: As a user, I want a one-word answer for the two obvious cases, so that I do not have to enumerate every number.
expected_behaviour: `parse_selection` returns every supported agent for `all` and an empty selection for `none`, both matched case-insensitively after trimming. `none` is a valid choice, not an error.
how_to_test: Run setup under a PTY answering `ALL`, confirm all agents are saved; rerun with a fresh HOME answering `None`, and confirm an empty agents list is saved without error.

feature_name: Invalid selections are rejected with an actionable message
user_story: As a user who mistypes, I want to be told what a valid answer looks like, so that I can correct it immediately.
expected_behaviour: An empty line, a non-numeric token, zero, or a number past `SUPPORTED_AGENTS.len()` all produce `SettingsError::InvalidSelection`, whose message names the accepted grammar: comma-separated numbers, `all`, or `none`.
how_to_test: Run setup under a PTY and answer in turn ``, `x`, `0`, and `99`; confirm each is refused and the error text names all three accepted forms.

feature_name: Settings are written atomically and never left half-written
user_story: As a user, I want an interrupted save to leave my previous settings intact, so that a crash cannot corrupt my configuration.
expected_behaviour: `save` writes to a pid-suffixed temporary file in the same directory with `create_new(true)`, fsyncs it, then `fs::rename`s it over the target. A reader therefore sees either the old file or the complete new one, never a truncated file.
how_to_test: Run setup to completion, then confirm `~/.resume/.settings-*.tmp` does not exist and `~/.resume/settings.json` parses as complete JSON.

feature_name: The settings file is created with owner-only permissions
user_story: As a user on a shared machine, I want my agent selection not to be world-readable, so that resume does not widen my exposure.
expected_behaviour: On Unix, `save` sets mode 0o600 on the temporary file before renaming it into place, so the settings file is readable and writable only by its owner.
how_to_test: Run setup, then `stat -f '%Lp' ~/.resume/settings.json` (macOS) and confirm it reports 600.

feature_name: Saved settings load back identically
user_story: As a returning user, I want my earlier selection honoured, so that setup is a one-time cost.
expected_behaviour: `load` parses the settings file, validates it, and returns a `Settings` equal to what `save` wrote, including the agent selection and the `known_agents` list.
how_to_test: Run setup selecting one agent, rerun `resume --list`, and confirm no prompt appears and only that agent's sessions are discovered.

feature_name: Malformed, wrong-version, or unknown-agent settings are refused
user_story: As a user with a hand-edited settings file, I want a clear error rather than silent misbehaviour, so that I can see my edit was wrong.
expected_behaviour: `Settings::validate` rejects any `schema_version` other than 1 with `UnsupportedSchema`, and any agent outside `SUPPORTED_AGENTS` with `UnknownAgent`; unparseable JSON produces `SettingsError::Parse` naming the path.
how_to_test: Write in turn `not json`, `{"schema_version",...}`, and `{"schema_version","agents":["unknown"],...}` to `~/.resume/settings.json`, run `resume --list` after each, and confirm each fails with a distinct, path-naming error.

feature_name: Agents added after setup are reported but not silently enabled
user_story: As a user upgrading resume, I want to learn that a new agent exists without it changing my scan set behind my back, so that upgrades are predictable.
expected_behaviour: `newly_supported` returns supported agents absent from the saved `known_agents`. `refresh_known_agents` appends them to `known_agents` and re-saves, but never adds them to `agents`, so the user's selection is unchanged until they opt in.
how_to_test: Hand-write a settings.json whose `known_agents` omits one supported agent, run `resume --list`, and confirm the new agent is reported, is not scanned, and that a second run reports nothing new.

feature_name: Unknown settings fields survive a rewrite
user_story: As a user on a mixed-version setup, I want fields written by a newer resume to survive an older one rewriting the file, so that downgrading does not destroy configuration.
expected_behaviour: `Settings` carries a `#[serde(flatten)] extra` map, so any field it does not recognize is preserved verbatim through load and save rather than dropped.
how_to_test: Add an unrecognized top-level key to settings.json, trigger a rewrite (by making `known_agents` stale so `refresh_known_agents` re-saves), and confirm the key survives with its value.

feature_name: `--list`/`--json` refuse to run setup non-interactively
user_story: As a script author, I want resume never to block on a prompt, so that automation cannot hang waiting for input.
expected_behaviour: `load_or_require_setup` returns `SettingsError::SetupRequired` when no settings file exists, instead of prompting. Its message tells the user to run `resume setup` in an interactive terminal.
how_to_test: With an isolated HOME lacking settings.json, run `resume --list < /dev/null` and confirm it exits with an error naming `resume setup` and does not block.

feature_name: Setup without a controlling terminal fails with a named cause
user_story: As a user running resume from a daemon or CI job, I want a specific error rather than a hang or a generic IO failure, so that the cause is obvious.
expected_behaviour: `run_setup` opens `/dev/tty` directly rather than reading stdin; when that fails it returns `SettingsError::NoTerminal`, whose message tells the user to run `resume setup` in an interactive terminal.
how_to_test: Run `resume setup` with the controlling terminal detached (for example under `setsid` with stdio redirected to files) and confirm the NoTerminal message rather than a hang.

feature_name: Settings live at ~/.resume/settings.json, ignoring XDG
user_story: As a user who relocated XDG_CONFIG_HOME, I want to know where resume keeps its agent selection, so that I can back it up or relocate it deliberately.
expected_behaviour: `settings_path` joins HOME with the fixed relative path `.resume/settings.json` and consults no XDG variable, unlike `config.rs`, which honours `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` for `config.toml`. The two mechanisms therefore resolve differently on the same machine.
how_to_test: Set XDG_CONFIG_HOME to a distinct directory, run setup, and confirm the file is written under `$HOME/.resume/`, not under XDG_CONFIG_HOME.

feature_name: Handoff is a no-op outside cmux
user_story: As an ordinary terminal user, I want resume to behave identically whether or not cmux exists on my machine, so that a workspace feature I do not use costs me nothing.
expected_behaviour: `handoff_cmux_workspace` returns `Ok()` immediately when neither `CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID` nor `CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set, without probing PATH for a `cmux` binary. Resume then execs the native agent exactly as it would without the feature.
how_to_test: With both cmux variables unset and no `cmux` on PATH, resume a session and confirm the agent is executed normally with no cmux-related output.

feature_name: Exactly one cmux identifier is an error, not a partial handoff
user_story: As a cmux user, I want a half-populated environment to stop resume rather than guess, so that a workspace is never pointed at the wrong session.
expected_behaviour: When one of `CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID`/`CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is present and the other is not, handoff returns `CmuxHandoffError::IncompleteEnv` and resume exits before exec. Provenance is never inferred from a single identifier.
how_to_test: Set only `CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID`, attempt a resume, and confirm exit 1 with an IncompleteEnv-derived message and that the agent was never executed.

feature_name: A cmux environment without the cmux CLI fails closed
user_story: As a cmux user, I want resume to refuse rather than resume without updating my workspace, so that the workspace never diverges from what is actually running.
expected_behaviour: With cmux identifiers present, `command_available` is consulted before any handoff work; a missing `cmux` binary yields `CmuxHandoffError::CliUnavailable` and resume exits 1 without exec.
how_to_test: Set both cmux variables with no `cmux` on PATH, attempt a resume, and confirm exit 1 and that the native agent was not executed.

feature_name: Workspace handoff completes before the agent is executed
user_story: As a cmux user, I want the workspace updated first, so that the resumed agent is never running under stale workspace state.
expected_behaviour: `handoff_then_exec` matches on `handoff_cmux_workspace` first and only reaches `exec` on `Ok()`. Because `exec` replaces the process image, any ordering inversion would be unobservable and unrecoverable — the ordering is therefore structural, not incidental.
how_to_test: With a fake `cmux` on PATH that appends to a log and a fake agent that appends to the same log, resume a session and confirm every cmux entry precedes the agent entry.

feature_name: The handoff verifies it is acting on its own caller
user_story: As a cmux user with several workspaces, I want resume to confirm which surface invoked it, so that it cannot retarget another workspace.
expected_behaviour: The handoff runs a cmux identify step and compares the reported caller against the environment-provided identifiers; a disagreement is `CmuxHandoffError::CallerMismatch` and exits before exec. Spawn failure, non-zero status, and unparseable JSON are separately reported as IdentifySpawn, IdentifyStatus, and IdentifyJson.
how_to_test: Drive the fake cmux to return in turn a mismatched caller, a non-zero exit, and malformed JSON; confirm each produces a distinct message and that the agent is never executed.

feature_name: An ambiguous workspace match aborts the handoff
user_story: As a cmux user, I want resume to refuse when it cannot identify exactly one target workspace, so that it never mutates an arbitrary one.
expected_behaviour: The workspace list step must resolve to exactly one workspace; zero or several yield `CmuxHandoffError::WorkspaceNotUnique` and exit 1 before exec. List spawn failure, non-zero status, and bad JSON map to ListSpawn, ListStatus, and ListJson.
how_to_test: Drive the fake cmux to list zero workspaces, then two matching workspaces, and confirm both abort before exec with a WorkspaceNotUnique-derived message.

feature_name: The workspace's pre-mutation state must match expectations
user_story: As a cmux user, I want resume to abort if the workspace already changed underneath it, so that it never overwrites a concurrent update.
expected_behaviour: Before reporting the new target, the handoff verifies the workspace's current state; a disagreement yields `CmuxHandoffError::PreStateMismatch` and exits before exec rather than clobbering the newer state.
how_to_test: Drive the fake cmux to report an unexpected pre-state and confirm the handoff aborts with exit 1 and no agent execution.

feature_name: The mutation is read back and verified before exec
user_story: As a cmux user, I want resume to confirm the workspace actually changed, so that a silently-ignored update cannot leave the workspace stale while the agent starts.
expected_behaviour: After the report step, the handoff reads the workspace back and compares it with the intended target; a mismatch is `CmuxHandoffError::ReadbackMismatch` and exits before exec. Report spawn failure and non-zero status map to ReportSpawn and ReportStatus.
how_to_test: Drive the fake cmux to accept the report but read back a different target, and confirm exit 1 with a ReadbackMismatch-derived message and no agent execution.

feature_name: An unavailable or non-UTF-8 target is refused
user_story: As a cmux user, I want resume to refuse a target it cannot faithfully transmit, so that the workspace never receives a mangled path.
expected_behaviour: A target that cannot be resolved yields `CmuxHandoffError::TargetUnavailable`; one that is not valid UTF-8 yields `NonUtf8Target`. Both exit before exec rather than passing a lossy value to cmux.
how_to_test: Resume a session whose recorded workspace path contains a non-UTF-8 byte under a cmux environment and confirm the NonUtf8Target path is taken rather than a lossy conversion.

feature_name: Every handoff failure mode exits 1 before exec
user_story: As a cmux user, I want no failure mode to fall through to a plain resume, so that fail-closed is a property of the design rather than of individual branches.
expected_behaviour: `CmuxHandoffError` declares 18 variants; `handoff_then_exec` reaches `exec` only on `Ok()`, so every one of them aborts before the process image is replaced. No variant has a fallback that resumes anyway.
how_to_test: Enumerate the variants from `src/launch.rs`, drive the fake cmux into each reachable one, and confirm every case exits 1 with the agent never executed.

feature_name: The picker offers an All tab plus one tab per present agent
user_story: As a user with several agents, I want to narrow the list to one agent without typing a filter, so that I can browse a single agent's history directly.
expected_behaviour: `run_tabbed_picker` builds tab 0 as All and tabs 1.. as each distinct agent in first-seen order over the rank-sorted snapshot. An agent contributing no Sessions gets no tab.
how_to_test: Under a PTY with fixture sessions for several agents, open the picker and confirm the header shows All plus exactly one tab per agent that has sessions.

feature_name: Six key bindings switch tabs, and they wrap
user_story: As a user, I want tab switching to respond to the keys my terminal actually sends, so that navigation works regardless of how my terminal encodes Alt-arrows.
expected_behaviour: `classify_nav` maps `Alt+Left`, `Left`, and `Shift+Tab` to the previous tab and `Alt+Right`, `Right`, and `Tab` to the next. Switching wraps modulo the tab count and resets the page to the tab's newest page.
how_to_test: Under a PTY, press each of the six keys in turn and confirm the header tab advances or retreats accordingly, wraps at both ends, and returns to page 1 after each switch.

feature_name: A growing tab list never retargets the current tab
user_story: As a user browsing one agent's tab while a background scan finishes, I want to stay on that tab, so that new results do not move me somewhere else.
expected_behaviour: The current tab is tracked by agent name, not index. When a background agent's first Session adds a new tab between renders, the name lookup still resolves to the same agent rather than shifting the user by one position.
how_to_test: Under a PTY with a slow Codex fixture, switch to a non-All tab before Codex finishes, wait for it to land, navigate once, and confirm the same agent tab is still selected.

feature_name: Alt+P and Alt+N move between older and newer pages
user_story: As a user with more sessions than fit on one page, I want to page through them, so that older sessions remain reachable.
expected_behaviour: `classify_nav` maps `Alt+P` to the older page and `Alt+N` to the newer one. Paging is clamped: Alt+P on the oldest page and Alt+N on the newest are no-ops that redraw the same page rather than wrapping.
how_to_test: Under a PTY with more than PAGE_SIZE fixture sessions, press Alt+P to the last page and once more, then Alt+N back to the first and once more, confirming both ends clamp.

feature_name: The newest page is always full; the remainder falls on the oldest page
user_story: As a user, I want my most recent sessions to fill the first screen, so that the common case is never a nearly-empty page.
expected_behaviour: `page_bounds` computes the page end as `total - page_index * PAGE_SIZE` and the start by saturating subtraction, so page 0 always holds the newest `PAGE_SIZE` entries and any short page is the oldest one.
how_to_test: With exactly PAGE_SIZE+3 fixture sessions, open the picker and confirm page 1 shows PAGE_SIZE rows and page 2 shows 3.

feature_name: A page index past the end is clamped, not left dangling
user_story: As a user switching to a tab with fewer pages, I want to land on a real page, so that the picker never shows an empty view.
expected_behaviour: Each render recomputes `total_pages` for the current tab and clamps `page_index` to `total_pages - 1`, so switching from a deep page of a large tab to a small tab lands on that tab's last page rather than beyond it.
how_to_test: Under a PTY, page deep into the All tab, switch to an agent tab with a single page, and confirm rows are shown rather than an empty page.

feature_name: Ctrl+O toggles the preview pane
user_story: As a user, I want to show or hide the preview without leaving the picker, so that I can trade screen space for detail on demand.
expected_behaviour: The picker binds `ctrl-o` to toggle-preview. The initial visibility follows the configured preview mode, and the pane position follows `preview_layout`: explicit right/bottom, or auto, which chooses right at terminal width 100 or more and bottom below that.
how_to_test: Under a PTY at width 120 and again at width 80, press Ctrl+O and confirm the pane appears on the right and at the bottom respectively, and that a second press hides it.

feature_name: Ctrl+R is inert in the picker
user_story: As a user with shell muscle memory, I want Ctrl+R not to disturb the picker, so that a reflexive keypress does not change my view.
expected_behaviour: The picker binds `ctrl-r:ignore`, so the key neither triggers Skim's default behaviour nor exits the picker; the current tab, page, and query are unchanged.
how_to_test: Under a PTY, type a query, press Ctrl+R, and confirm the query, tab, and page are unchanged and the picker is still running.

feature_name: An empty candidate list waits for a running background scan
user_story: As a user whose only sessions come from Codex, I want to be told resume is still scanning rather than shown an empty picker, so that I do not think I have no sessions.
expected_behaviour: When the candidate list is empty and a `BackgroundAgent` is still pending, `run_tabbed_picker` prints `resume: waiting for <agent> to finish scanning...` once and polls until a candidate arrives. With no pending background agent and no candidates it returns Cancelled instead of opening an empty picker.
how_to_test: Under a PTY with a fixture where only Codex has sessions and its scan is slow, confirm the waiting line is printed exactly once and the picker then opens with rows.

feature_name: Rows are ordered oldest-first with the most recent at the bottom
user_story: As a user, I want the most recently active session nearest my cursor, so that the common choice needs the least movement.
expected_behaviour: The snapshot is sorted ascending by `PickerCandidate::rank` with the candidate key as a stable tiebreak, mirroring `session::compare_sessions` reversed. The most recently active session is therefore the bottom row of the newest page.
how_to_test: Under a PTY with fixture sessions of known activity times, confirm the bottom row of page 1 is the most recently active and that reruns produce an identical order.

feature_name: Codex scans in the background when other agents are configured
user_story: As a user with a large Codex corpus, I want the picker to open on my other agents immediately, so that Codex's slow scan does not hold the whole tool closed.
expected_behaviour: `run_interactive` sets `codex_async` when Codex is configured alongside at least one other agent. Codex then discovers on a detached thread while the picker opens on the synchronous agents' results.
how_to_test: With fixtures for Codex and at least one other agent, run `resume` under a PTY and confirm the picker opens before Codex's scan completes.
spec_ref: §5 Codex parallel scan and discovery cache

feature_name: Codex stays synchronous when it is the only agent
user_story: As a user who configured only Codex, I want resume to wait rather than show me an empty picker, so that backgrounding does not produce a useless view.
expected_behaviour: `codex_async` requires more than one configured agent, so `-a codex` alone discovers synchronously exactly like every other agent.
how_to_test: Run `resume -a codex` under a PTY and confirm the picker does not open until Codex's scan has finished.
spec_ref: §5 Codex parallel scan and discovery cache

feature_name: Background Codex results appear on the next navigation
user_story: As a user, I want Codex sessions to show up once its scan finishes, so that backgrounding does not lose results.
expected_behaviour: `merge_records` appends into the shared candidate list, and `run_tabbed_picker` re-reads that snapshot on every page turn and tab switch — but never mid-render, so rows never shift under the cursor.
how_to_test: Under a PTY, open the picker before Codex finishes, wait for it to complete, press Tab, and confirm Codex sessions and its tab are now present.
spec_ref: §5 Codex parallel scan and discovery cache

feature_name: The Codex timing line is deferred until the picker releases the terminal
user_story: As a user, I want no stray output over the picker's rendering, so that the display is never corrupted.
expected_behaviour: Codex's elapsed-time line is buffered on a channel and flushed only after `run_tabbed_picker` returns, using `try_recv` so a still-running scan prints nothing rather than blocking.
how_to_test: Under a PTY, confirm no `resume: codex scanned` line appears while the picker is drawn, and that it appears afterwards when the scan finished first and not at all when the user acted first.

feature_name: Rollout parsing is parallel above a threshold and bounded
user_story: As a user with thousands of rollout files, I want discovery to use several cores without exhausting them, so that resume is fast without destabilizing my machine.
expected_behaviour: `parallel_map` fans out only when the item count reaches `PARALLEL_THRESHOLD` (16) and never spawns more than `MAX_DISCOVERY_WORKERS` (8) scoped threads; below the threshold it runs serially, avoiding thread setup cost for small corpora.
how_to_test: Time `resume --json -a codex` against a fixture with several hundred rollouts and confirm it completes without spawning an unbounded number of threads; confirm a 3-file fixture returns the same sessions.
spec_ref: §5 Codex parallel scan and discovery cache

feature_name: An unchanged rollout file is served from the discovery cache
user_story: As a returning user, I want the second run to be faster than the first, so that repeated use is cheap.
expected_behaviour: `DiscoveryCache::lookup` returns the recorded outcome when the file's size and mtime both still match, skipping the read and JSON parse entirely. The rollout JSONL remains authoritative; the cache only avoids re-deriving what it already holds.
how_to_test: Run `resume --json -a codex` twice against an unchanged large fixture and confirm the second run is faster and returns byte-identical JSON.
spec_ref: §5 Codex parallel scan and discovery cache

feature_name: A missing, corrupt, or stale-version cache degrades to a full scan
user_story: As a user, I want a damaged cache never to change my results, so that a speed optimization cannot become a correctness problem.
expected_behaviour: `DiscoveryCache::load` treats a missing file, unreadable file, malformed JSON, and a `version` other than `CACHE_VERSION` all as an empty cache rather than an error, so discovery silently falls back to a full fresh scan. Deleting the cache file is always safe.
how_to_test: Run once to populate the cache, then in turn truncate it, fill it with garbage, and rewrite its version field; after each, confirm `resume --json -a codex` returns the same sessions as a cold run and reports no error.
spec_ref: §5 Codex parallel scan and discovery cache

feature_name: The discovery cache honours XDG_CACHE_HOME
user_story: As a user, I want the cache in my configured cache directory, so that it is covered by my existing cleanup and backup rules.
expected_behaviour: `cache_path` returns `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/resume/codex-discovery-v1.json` when XDG_CACHE_HOME is set, otherwise `~/.cache/resume/codex-discovery-v1.json`. It reads no environment variable directly, so callers and tests can inject isolation.
how_to_test: Set XDG_CACHE_HOME to a fixture directory, run `resume --json -a codex`, and confirm the cache file is created there and not under HOME.
spec_ref: §5 Codex parallel scan and discovery cache

feature_name: Cache entries for deleted rollouts under the current root are pruned
user_story: As a user who cleans up old Codex rollouts, I want the cache not to grow forever, so that it does not accumulate dead entries indefinitely.
expected_behaviour: `save` drops any entry whose path is under the current run's effective root but was not seen this run — the file no longer exists, since caching means every current file under that root is enumerated.
how_to_test: Populate the cache from a fixture, delete one rollout file, rerun `resume --json -a codex`, and confirm the cache file no longer contains that path.
spec_ref: §5 Codex parallel scan and discovery cache

feature_name: Entries from a different CODEX_HOME are never treated as orphaned
user_story: As a user who switches between Codex homes, I want each home's cache to survive runs against the other, so that alternating does not repeatedly cold-start.
expected_behaviour: `save` prunes only entries under the *current* effective root. An entry under a different root is left untouched, because this run scanned only its own root and has no evidence about anything outside it.
how_to_test: Run against CODEX_HOME A, then against CODEX_HOME B, and confirm the cache still contains A's entries; run against A again and confirm it is a warm run.
spec_ref: §5 Codex parallel scan and discovery cache

feature_name: A scope-rejected file is never cached as having no session
user_story: As a user running resume from different directories, I want scope to affect only what is listed, so that a narrow run cannot poison later broader runs.
expected_behaviour: Only a full, ungated parse is recorded. A Scope's early workspace-gate rejection is a fact about that run's Scope, not about the file, so caching it as NoSession would make a later broader run wrongly believe the file holds no Session. A parse error is likewise never cached.
how_to_test: Run `resume --json -a codex` from a narrow scope that excludes a known session, then rerun with `-D all` from the same HOME, and confirm the excluded session is listed.
spec_ref: §5 Codex parallel scan and discovery cache

feature_name: OMP workspace directories are prefiltered without reading files
user_story: As a user with many OMP workspaces, I want discovery to skip irrelevant directories cheaply, so that scoping is fast.
expected_behaviour: OMP encodes home-relative workspace paths as dash-prefixed directory names. Discovery keeps only names starting with `-` that pass `scope::may_contain_session_dir`, which compares lossy keys of the directory name against the scope's candidate keys — no file inside a rejected directory is ever opened.
how_to_test: With OMP fixture workspaces both inside and outside the current scope, run `resume --json -a omp` and confirm only in-scope workspaces contribute sessions.

feature_name: Workspaces under hidden dot directories are matched
user_story: As a user whose worktrees live under a dot directory, I want their sessions found, so that hidden paths are not silently invisible.
expected_behaviour: `lossy_key` maps every non-alphanumeric character to `-`, so a leading dot in a path segment collapses like any other separator and a workspace under a hidden directory produces a key that still prefix-matches its scope.
how_to_test: Create an OMP fixture whose workspace path contains a hidden dot directory, run `resume --json -a omp` from that workspace, and confirm the session is listed.

feature_name: The spec's claim about RESUME_* environment variables matches the code
user_story: As a user reading the design document, I want its environment-variable claims to be true, so that I can rely on the document when auditing what resume reads.
expected_behaviour: docs/product-design.md:515 states there are no custom `RESUME_*` environment variables and that only standard HOME/XDG/PATH and official agent variables are read. `proc::snapshot` reads `RESUME_DISABLE_PROC_PROBE` on the production path, and `codex::activity` reads the same constant, so the claim and the code must be reconciled.
how_to_test: `grep -rn 'RESUME_' src --include='*.rs'` and confirm every production hit is either absent or documented in docs/product-design.md.
fix_ref: docs/product-design.md: replaced the "no custom RESUME_* variables" claim with the actual contract for RESUME_DISABLE_PROC_PROBE

feature_name: The settings.json mechanism is described in the design document
user_story: As a user, I want every file resume reads or writes under my home directory to be documented, so that no configuration surface is invisible.
expected_behaviour: docs/product-design.md §7 documents `config.toml` and its XDG resolution. `~/.resume/settings.json` is a second, separate mechanism that stores the agent selection, resolves via HOME only, and is created by `resume setup`; the document must describe it for the configuration surface to be complete.
how_to_test: Search docs/product-design.md for `settings.json` and `resume setup` and confirm both the file, its location, and the setup command are described.
fix_ref: docs/product-design.md (### Agent selection): new subsection covering ~/.resume/settings.json, its schema, the resume setup chooser, the atomic 0600 write, the new-agent notification, and -a/config precedence

feature_name: Every bound tab-switching key is documented
user_story: As a user, I want the documented keys to match the bound keys, so that the document is a reliable reference.
expected_behaviour: docs/product-design.md:281 describes tab and page navigation. `classify_nav` binds six tab keys (Alt+Left, Left, Shift+Tab, Alt+Right, Right, Tab) and two page keys (Alt+P, Alt+N); the document must list what is actually bound.
how_to_test: Compare the key list at docs/product-design.md:281 against the match arms in `classify_nav` and confirm they agree in both directions.
fix_ref: docs/product-design.md: the tab-key sentence now states that Left/Shift+Tab and Right/Tab are equivalent to the Alt-arrow bindings

feature_name: `--version` prints the crate version and exits 0
user_story: As a user reporting a bug, I want to state which resume I am running, so that the report is actionable.
expected_behaviour: `-V`/`--version` is clap's standard version action, wired from the crate version, and prints `resume <semver>` to stdout with exit code 0 without performing any discovery.
how_to_test: Run `resume --version` and confirm stdout matches `resume <major>.<minor>.<patch>`, exit code 0, and that no diagnostics are printed.

feature_name: An unparseable `--since` value is a usage error
user_story: As a user who mistypes a cutoff, I want to be told what forms are accepted, so that I can correct it without reading the manual.
expected_behaviour: `Since::from_str` rejects anything that is not a duration (`7d`, `2h`, `30m`, `1w`), a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, or `all`. clap surfaces the rejection as exit code 2 with a message naming all three accepted forms, matching error catalog entry E1001 INVALID_SINCE.
how_to_test: Run `resume --since nope --list` and confirm exit code 2 and a stderr message naming duration, YYYY-MM-DD, and `all`.

feature_name: `--help` names every supported agent
user_story: As a user deciding whether resume covers my agent, I want `--help` to list the agents it actually scans, so that I do not conclude mine is unsupported.
expected_behaviour: The `long_about` prose that feeds `--help`, and the same paragraph in the man page, describe which agents resume scans. That list must match `cli::SUPPORTED_AGENTS`, or a user of a supported agent is told their agent is not covered.
how_to_test: Run `resume --help` and confirm every entry of `SUPPORTED_AGENTS` appears in the prose; repeat for `resume --man`.
fix_ref: src/cli.rs (long_about) + src/man.rs: both agent lists now name OpenCode
